jobs.title: Cable Splicer - Outside Plant (OSP)
jobs.description:
Link Solutions is seeking a Cable Splicer Outside Plant (OSP) to join our team at Fort Stewart/Hunter Army Airfield, GA

• Must be a U.S. Citizen
• Requires a DoD Secret Clearance (clearance sponsorship available for qualified candidates).
• Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
• Non-remote (relocation incentive available)

The Cable Splicer (OSP) will play a critical role in supporting and maintaining the telecommunications infrastructure serving the Southeast Region Cyber Support Center (SE RCSC). In this position, you will install, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair fiber optic, copper, and coaxial cable systems that enable secure voice and data communications for mission-essential operations.

This role offers the opportunity to work on a diverse communications network supporting Department of Defense initiatives while utilizing advanced telecommunications technologies and industry-leading practices. The ideal candidate is a hands-on telecommunications professional who enjoys solving technical challenges, working outdoors, and contributing to systems that support national defense missions.

Job Responsibilities:

• Install, splice, terminate, test, troubleshoot, and repair fiber optic, copper, and coaxial cable systems supporting telecommunications infrastructure.
• Perform routine preventive maintenance and corrective maintenance activities to ensure optimal network performance and reliability.
• Locate, diagnose, and resolve cable faults, service interruptions, and connectivity issues.
• Install, maintain, and repair aerial, underground, and direct-buried communication cable systems.
• Perform fusion and mechanical fiber splicing and conduct testing using OTDRs, power meters, and other telecommunications test equipment.
• Read, interpret, and update cable records, engineering drawings, schematics, splice diagrams, and as-built documentation.
• Conduct cable audits and infrastructure inspections of manholes, handholes, pedestals, telecommunications closets, MDFs, IDFs, and outside plant facilities.
• Maintain telephone poles, conduit systems, manholes, handholes, and outside plant distribution equipment.
• Support cable route planning, cable placement, and infrastructure upgrades to improve network performance and capacity.
• Collaborate with government customers to identify operational requirements and recommend telecommunications infrastructure improvements.
• Respond to service requests and ensure assigned work orders and trouble tickets are completed accurately and within established timelines.
• Ensure compliance with BICSI standards, OSHA regulations, DoD requirements, and industry best practices.
• Maintain accurate work documentation, inspection records, cable inventories, and project status reports.
• Support telecommunications modernization efforts and infrastructure expansion projects.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job.

Compensation:

• $29.42 per hour
• Full-Time (Monday-Friday)

This position is covered by the Service Contract Act (SCA). Compensation and benefits are provided in accordance with applicable wage determinations and contract requirements. Please see the Additional Information section below for benefit details.

• U.S. Citizen.
• Actice DoD Secret Clearance (clearance sponsorship available for qualified candidates).
• Five (5+) years of experience installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing outside plant (OSP) telecommunications infrastructure.
• Experience with fiber optic, copper, and coaxial cable systems, including installation, testing, and repair.
• Experience working with aerial, underground, and direct-buried cable plant environments.
• Experience reading and interpreting telecommunications drawings, cable records, splice diagrams, and technical documentation.
• Knowledge of BICSI standards, telecommunications installation practices, and industry regulations.
• Knowledge of OSHA safety requirements and telecommunications industry best practices.
• Experience utilizing telecommunications test equipment, including OTDRs, optical power meters, cable analyzers, and fault-locating equipment.
• Ability to work independently and troubleshoot telecommunications infrastructure issues in a field environment.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
• Valid driver's license and ability to operate company vehicles (acceptable driving record only).

Preferred:

• Experience supporting Department of Defense (DoD), Federal Government, or military telecommunications infrastructure.
• Experience performing fiber optic fusion splicing, termination, testing, and troubleshooting.
• BICSI Installer, BICSI Technician, or other telecommunications industry certifications.
• FOA Certified Fiber Optic Technician (CFOT) or equivalent fiber optic certification.
• OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 Certification.
• Experience maintaining as-built documentation, infrastructure records, and cable plant inventories.
• Experience supporting telecommunications infrastructure upgrades, modernization efforts, and expansion projects.
• Experience working with manholes, handholes, pedestals, duct banks, and outside plant distribution systems.
• Strong customer service, communication, and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to prioritize multiple work assignments in a fast-paced mission environment.

This position is covered under the Service Contract Act (SCA) and includes a comprehensive benefits package.

• Eligible employees receive Health & Welfare (H&W) benefits in accordance with applicable SCA requirements.
• Employees accrue paid sick leave based on hours worked, up to the applicable annual limit.
• Paid vacation is available based on length of qualifying service, with additional time earned at designated service milestones.
• Employees receive paid federal holidays in accordance with applicable requirements.

Benefits are provided in accordance with applicable Service Contract Act wage determinations and contract requirements.

Link Solutions, Inc. is an EOE. AA/M/F/D/V. We participate in the E-Verify Employment Verification Program. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Regional Operations Manager
jobs.description:
The Regional Operations Manager will manage and coordinate staff and operations of inside sales, warehouse, inventory, seal repair, machining, assembly, CAD engineering and procurement to achieve timely production of quality products at the most economical cost and proper quantities.  Develop and coordinate a work force capable of meeting the operating procedures to facilitate the physical distribution of product.

SPECIFIC DUTIES, ACTIVITIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:

* Supervise work of personnel; schedule work, manage overtime, cross train, and manage personnel actions.

* Provides leadership for team through effective communications, coaching, training, and development.

* Develops and monitors operating procedures in order processing, inventory control, customer service, seal repair, machining, assembly, etc. and personnel training.

* Handles incoming telephone, fax, mail orders and inquires on a variety of subject matters such as pricing    information and quotations, part identification, application recommendations, delivery dates, change orders and seal repair service.

* Interprets and implements company policies.

* Manages inventory management system to optimize customer order requirements while maintaining capacity utilization and the lowest level of inventory.

* Approves ordering parts from vendors.  Authorizes substitute part numbers.

* Achieves monthly forecasts, backlog management, and on-time delivery.

* Manages annual operating budgets.  Oversees the maintenance of building, equipment, grounds, etc.

* Analyzes operations problems or deficiencies and initiates corrective action.

* Provides assurance that safety, health and environmental rules and regulations are met or exceeded.

Additional duties as assigned.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS:

* Bachelor’s degree in a business-related field preferred or equivalent work experience.

* Minimum 6 years working in a manufacturing environment to include mechanical seals or rotating equipment, inventory, material management, and distribution practices.

* Must be able to read blueprints.

* Supervisory experience to include supervising a diverse work force.

* Knowledge of integrated business and manufacturing systems operations involving MRP.

* Knowledge of Continuous Improvement Process (CIP).

* Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to effectively communicate with all levels within the organization.

* Ability to work a flexible schedule as needed to accommodate business operations.

* Machine shop experience is a big plus.

EHS REQUIREMENTS:

* Completes all work in a safe manner and follow all safety requirements consistently by supporting the company’s goals.

* Lifting guidelines in accordance with the Manual Lifting Guidelines noted in the Safety Handbook.

* Follows all environmental requirements consistently by supporting the company’s environmental performance goals.

jobs.title: Senior Applications Chemist, Eurofins Environment Testing Air Toxics, Folsom, CA
jobs.description:
Eurofins Environment Testing is seeking a Senior Applications Chemist to join our team! The Senior Applications Chemist functions as a subject matter expert for GC and GC/MS technology within Eurofins Environmental Testing, supporting multiple projects, clients, and laboratory teams through advanced troubleshooting, method optimization, and technical leadership.

Key Responsibilities

• Act as the primary technical authority for GC and GC/MS instrumentation and applications.
• Lead investigations of complex analytical issues affecting data quality or turnaround time.
• Support method development, modification, and validation projects in response to new client needs or regulatory changes.
• Establish and promote best practices for instrument maintenance, system cleanliness, and performance monitoring.
• Partner with QA, operations, and leadership to support continuous improvement and standardization across Eurofins laboratories.
• Support client technical discussions and respond to inquiries requiring advanced analytical knowledge.
• Contribute to evaluation and implementation of new instrumentation, consumables, and technologies.
• Provide advanced training and mentorship to lab teams.

Basic Minimum Qualifications

• BS or MS in Chemistry or related discipline.
• Extensive experience with GC/MS platforms including GC/MS/MS.
• Demonstrated leadership in method development and technical problem solving.
• Experience with air-phase analysis and EPA Toxic Organic Compendium methods preferred.
• Experience mentoring teams and influencing across functions.
• Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
• Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English

Compensation: $75,000 - $95,000 per year.

This position is exempt from overtime with Full-time hours, Monday - Friday, 8am - 5pm.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base compensation may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base compensation of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work.  We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

We support your development! Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity! Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us! We are well on our way to achieving our objective of carbon neutrality by 2025, through a combination of emission reduction and compensation initiatives. We encourage our laboratory leaders to make sustainable changes at their local level, and in addition to their initiatives we also count on our dedicated carbon reduction team to help us to achieve this goal!

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

Eurofins USA Environment Testing is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

jobs.description:
The Field Technician position is responsible for the pick-up and delivery of water, soil and air samples to and from the laboratory. • Prepare and deliver bottle orders to clients following the standard operating procedure of the lab.

• Pick up and deliver samples, bottle orders and report to the laboratory for sign-in and analysis.

• Maintain delivery truck to keep in proper working order.
• Label samples after log in on an as needed basis.
• Perform all duties as outlined in the Standard Operating Procedure for Couriers

Education: High school diploma or equivalent

Experience: None required.

• Valid driver's license required without recent incident. Will drive a company vehicle as needed.

This isn’t your typical sales role, and it is not a pure lead-generation or hunting position. It is the perfect stepping stone for an ambitious professional who wants to master the operational side of complex, enterprise-level fintech deals before transitioning into a full Business Development role.

You will act as the crucial connective tissue between our Business Development (BD) team, internal stakeholders, and prospective partners. By anticipating needs, managing cross-functional workflows, and owning deal governance, you will free up our BDs to do what they do best: sell. You won't just be taking orders; you will be the engine room of the deal-flow process, driving velocity, reducing time-to-revenue, and increasing conversion rates.

Your Mission:

• Top-of-Funnel Support: Collaborate with BDs to research target accounts, build stakeholder maps, and create intelligence briefs to inform initial marketing and sales outreach.
• Deal Project Management: Own the project plan for active opportunities. Assign action items, hold internal and external owners accountable, and manage risk registers to prevent deal slippage.
• Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner with Compliance, Product, Legal, and Operations to drive due diligence, RFI/RFP responses, and complex partner onboarding workflows.
• Opportunity Conversion: Prepare introductory materials, customize engaging sales collateral, and run data analysis on payment routes for prospective partners.
• Deal Governance: Maintain pristine Salesforce data, ensure stage gates are followed correctly, and drive internal communication via dedicated opportunity Slack channels.

• Proactive Problem Solver: You don't wait to be told what to do. You naturally anticipate the needs of a busy BD team, identify process gaps, and offer solutions before being asked.
• Future BD Manager: You have the ambition and sales mindset to eventually transition into a full Enterprise Business Development role, using this position to master the lifecycle of complex sales.
• Strategic Sales Background: A proven track record in sales development (BDR/SDR), sales enablement, or revenue strategy, with a clear understanding that this role extends far beyond just outreach.
• Detail-Oriented & Organized: You thrive in a complex environment, easily managing multiple workstreams, RFPs, and deal flow stages simultaneously without letting details slip.
• Cross-Functional Collaborator: You excel at bringing diverse groups together and navigating internal teams to achieve a shared goal.
• Analytically Astute: You have the ability to interpret large volumes of data and translate it into actionable insights for the sales team.
• Tech-Savvy: You are highly comfortable navigating modern revenue tech stacks. Experience with Salesforce and HubSpot is a strong plus.

jobs.title: Compliance Senior Manager- Fraud Investigations
jobs.description:
Wise is looking for a Senior Manager to join its growing financial crime compliance oversight team in North America. This role will be working alongside the NorthAm Financial Crime Compliance Lead and a highly effective team in second line compliance.

In this role you will be responsible for the effective mitigation of financial crime risks for our onboarding and ongoing customer due diligence program. This position requires close partnership with our financial crime compliance operational and product teams, with opportunities to present to senior stakeholders and shape the strategic direction of the financial crime compliance program.

Your Mission:

• Supervision of our appropriate measures to ensure that Financial crime risks are taken into account in our day-to-day operations with a focus on AML and Fraud investigations
• Provide advice and guidance to other teams and key stakeholders both regionally and globally, on BSA and AML/CTF regulations as well as related Wise policies and procedures for Wise US Inc and Wise Canada
• Support in the development and maintenance of the compliance FinCrime oversight framework specifically on AML and Fraud investigations and controls
• Challenge first line teams on the development of controls and provide approvals on any control changes, new products or features
• Represent fincrime compliance oversight both internally and externally to regulators, auditors and partners as required showcasing Wise’s strong oversight compliance framework
• Ensuring that there is strong oversight of all compliance operations focusing on AML and Fraud
• Serve as a member of the US SAR committee, providing feedback to our SAR Reporting Team
• Contribute to the company’s annual Financial Crime Risk Assessment for Wise US Inc.
• Horizon scanning of new FinCrime regulatory developments and maintaining oversight of implementation of such development which impact business activities
• Proactively identifying key areas of risk and work with first line teams in the development of mitigation plans as needed
• Define and monitor MI/KRIs for the covered areas (quality, timeliness, backlog health, decision consistency, SAR outcomes), escalating concerns with clear recommendations.

A Bit About You:

• Theory. You are an expert in US financial crime regulations including the Bank Secrecy Act, OFAC, NY DFS Part 504, and may be currently working or have worked within the area of financial crime compliance preferably in a fast paced environment either at financial institution, fintech, money service business or as a consultant. You have extensive experience working on AML and Fraud investigations.

• Communication. You are a comfortable and effective communicator in both your writing and speaking. You can convey complex ideas effectively to both internal and external audiences.

• Team player. You have great people skills and can effectively and efficiently collaborate, build relationships with colleagues throughout the business and across the globe.
• Travel. You must be willing to travel to our other offices as required.
• Must already be legally authorized to work in the US, we cannot provide Visas for this role
• This is NOT a remote position, this is a full-time position that will be located in New York, NY. Wise requires three days of in-office work.

Nice to haves:

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
KIPP TEAM & Family’s Data, Technology and Innovation Team (DTI) seeks a Data Analyst to develop and maintain trusted dashboards and reports across academics, student operations and enrollment, and compliance. You will work directly with leaders to build data products that help our students on their path to college, careers and choice-filled lives.

Our stack includes SQL, dbt, the Cube semantic layer, Tableau, Git and Claude, to name a few. Our analytics engineering work runs through an AI-assisted development workflow with version control and code review. Over the next year, we plan to replace Tableau with BI-as-code tools, and you will help shape that shift.

Here's what you'll be doing:

Build Trusted Data Products (60%)

• Develop and maintain dashboards and reports across academic, enrollment and compliance data, with an equity lens
• Help lead our move from Tableau to BI-as-code tools
• Create documentation and training that drive consistent, confident use and scalable development

Develop and Maintain Data Models (25%)

• Build, test and document dbt models and Cube semantic-layer metrics in our shared repository
• Ship work through our development cycle: branches, pull requests, code review and automated checks
• Use AI-assisted tools like Claude to work faster, while verifying every output and protecting student privacy

Support Users and Drive Improvement Cycles (15%)

• Work directly with stakeholders, from teachers to board members, to integrate their feedback and build data products people can use effectively
• Manage life cycle of project intake and request tracking for data products

Must Haves

• Love of data, problem-solving, and collaboration, and a drive to learn
• A proven record of building trust with a wide range of teammates
• Deep commitment to both racial and educational equity
• Strong SQL skills
• Experience with Tableau or other business intelligence tools
• Experience with K-12 academic or operations data
• Clear writing and communication, and attention to detail that protects data integrity
• Model KIPP TEAM & Family’s Be The Change values: Kid Focus, Radical Love, Excellence, Team & Fun

Preferred

• 3+ years in a K-12 school operations, data, or technology role
• Experience with dbt or a similar transformation framework, or with a semantic layer such as Cube
• Comfort with Git and GitHub workflows: pull requests, code review and CI/CD
• Hands-on experience with AI-assisted coding tools (e.g., Claude Code)
• Experience with BI-as-code tools or Python for data work
• Experience with a cloud data warehouse (BigQuery preferred)
• Experience with student enrollment or state compliance reporting

Location

This is a hybrid role. At this time, we typically work on-site 2 days per week and work remotely 3 days per week. Therefore, this role requires teammates to live within commuting distance of one of the three cities within which we work: Newark, NJ, Camden, NJ, or Miami, FL. Candidates who can work from our Newark office will be given preference for this role.

Compensation & Benefits

KIPP Team & Family offers a market-competitive salary range of $85,000 - $115,000. Salary ranges at KIPP are set based upon the role level and function using benchmarks in the education and non-profit sector and allow for growth within the role.  Individual compensation within this range will be set  based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to: relevant professional experience and qualifications; education, skills and training; and market conditions.

In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a generous benefits package including, but not limited to, the following:

• Robust benefits that include medical, dental, and vision

• Demonstrates strong technical aptitude with the ability to learn complex systems, tools, and testing methodologies.
• Communicates clearly and professionally with a wide range of stakeholders, from engineers and technicians to senior leaders at customer sites.
• Builds strong relationships; is comfortable in customer-facing situations; and handles rejection and setbacks with resilience and maturity.
• Shows adaptability, humility, and a willingness to “do what it takes,” from detailed preparation and follow-up to on-site plant visits and presentations.

jobs.title: Operations Support Specialist
jobs.description:
The Operations Support Specialist plays a critical role in maintaining the pristine environment required for semiconductor manufacturing. This position focuses on the meticulous daily sanitation of wafer fab facilities, processing specialized cleanroom garments, and keeping essential production supplies fully stocked. This is a vital execution role that ensures the production floor remains compliant with strict cleanliness regulations.

Key Responsibilities

• Sanitation: Mop floors and wipe down walls, workstations, and external machine surfaces using cleanroom procedures and approved chemical solutions.
• Garment Management: Collect, wash, inspect, and organize specialized cleanroom garments (bunny suits, hoods, and boots) to ensure an uninterrupted supply for the manufacturing shifts.
• Consumable Stocking: Monitor and replenish cleanroom gowning area supplies, including face masks, gloves, hairnets, shoe covers, and lint-free wipes.
• Waste Removal: Safely collect and empty trash, recycling, and non-hazardous waste bins from the gowning rooms and production corridors according to protocol.
• Protocol Compliance: Strictly follow all cleanroom entry, exit, and safety protocols, including wearing cleanroom garments and required protective gear.
• Miscellaneous: Other various responsibilities to keep manufacturing areas clean and well organized.

Required Skills & Qualifications

• Education: High School Diploma or equivalent.
• Experience: Previous experience in commercial cleaning, janitorial work, or warehouse stocking is preferred; specific cleanroom training will be provided on the job.
• Attention to Detail: Ability to follow highly specific, step-by-step cleaning procedures.
• Physical Stamina: Ability to stand, walk, bend, and lift up to 35 lbs throughout a shift while wearing a protective cleanroom suit.
• Reliability: Strong punctuality and dependability to ensure the fab remains clean and stocked for continuous 24/7 manufacturing operations.

Due to the nature of this position and the required access to areas where ITAR-controlled articles and/or technical data may be present, candidates must meet the applicable U.S. person requirements for ITAR access. This includes individuals who are:

• A lawful permanent resident (Green Card holder); or

A protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3).

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician I
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

Performs maintenance services, installation or repairs in one or more skill areas such as plumbing, mechanical, electrical repairs, pneumatic, hydraulic, installation, carpentry, painting or vehicle servicing.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Performs routine and preventative maintenance, lubrication and minor adjustments on machines and related equipment which may include pumps, engines, centrifuges, generators, valves, gates, mixers, conveyors, blowers, dryers, chemical feed and odor control, disinfection equipment, vacuum filters and belt presses. Promptly reports any operational problems with machines or equipment to Lead or Supervisor.
• Learns to inspect and becomes proficient at mechanical troubleshooting to determine repairs needed. Dismantles equipment to gain access to and repairs defective parts using hand tools, power tools and precision measuring and testing devices. Re-assembles and tests equipment ensuring safe and efficient operating conditions are restored. Learns to troubleshoot hydraulic, pneumatic and electronic equipment and instrumentation.
• Performs facility maintenance and repair and may replace or install light bulbs, fluorescent tubes, damaged glass, windows, doors, partitions, ceiling or floor tiles, door locks, carpet, and/or paint.
• May perform manual labor including cleaning equipment, facilities and grounds as required and properly disposes of waste according to safety and environmental policies. Operates vehicles for plant operational purposes.
• Learns to estimate time and material costs for various projects. May assist in other areas of plant as directed.

Work Environment:

• Spends 100% of the time in the operations environment.
• Typically spends 25 – 35% of time exposed to outdoor and sometimes inclement weather.
• Company service vehicles are used as required.
• Travels 1 – 2 times per year for company provided training.
• May serve rotational 24-hour emergency on call.
• Possible Work Hazards: May be exposed to possible operations hazards including fumes, dust, toxic and caustic chemicals, noise, rotating machinery, high pressure and hot and cold temperatures, slippery surfaces, water and electrical hazards.

Education/Experience/Background:

• High School Diploma or GED with the ability to read, write and comprehend English (operational, process, safety and quality instructions) and be able to carry out verbal and written instructions.
• Six months to two years of experience in a related position with ability to comprehend specifications, blueprints and manuals.
• Experience using power, pneumatic, hydraulic, and hand tools and shop tools such as drill press, band saw, bench grinder, and torque wrench preferred.
• Experience using material handling equipment, pressure gauges and precision measuring instruments.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

• Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations.
• Must have ability to operate Computer Maintenance Management System (software).
• Must consistently demonstrate the ability to learn and independently perform assigned duties and meet or exceed production and quality goals.
• Must demonstrate ability to work in a team environment and willingness to assume additional or new responsibilities readily.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

• Some vocational training and mechanical aptitude preferred, with the ability to read, interpret and record data from meters, gauges, scales, panels, computer consoles and other equipment.
• Minimum water / wastewater license as required by regulatory agency at site.
• Must possess a valid driver’s license and a safe driving record.
• Employee Orientation, Departmental Operating Procedures, Safety, Confined Space training, OSHA and Quality Training.
• HAZWOPER (Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response) Level I and II First Responder Certification if required by site.
• Minimum water / wastewater operator state certification.
• Must become proficient in the care and use of all site specific, facility required PPE (Personal Protection Equipment), including respirators, gas detectors, confined space equipment, etc.)
• Forklift Certification if required by site.
• Training in operation of mechanical drives, hydraulic pumps and valves, pneumatics, electronics and control systems.
• Obtain or maintain HVAC, Electrician, Plumber’s or other trade License if assigned to that area.
• Note: Tech will not perform duties unless properly licensed.
• Training in the use of energy management systems as needed.
• Works toward increasing skills in additional functional areas or in obtaining advanced skills / maintenance certifications.

Physical Requirements:

• Amount of time spent – Standing 25%, Walking 75% for as many as five miles per shift.
• Requires close visual and hearing observation to detect non-conformance and machine malfunction.
• Constantly uses hands to finger, handle or feel and frequently reaches with hands and arms.
• Works in various positions; works on ladders, catwalks, and supports at heights of 50 feet above the ground; and works with hands extended above and below head and body up to 40 minutes using hand tools weighing up to 15 pounds.
• Must be able to lift and carry 50 pounds (occasionally 60 pounds) distances of 10 feet.

The Associate Attorney - Condo/Co-Op serves as a trusted advisor to cooperative and condominium boards and managing agents, while also handling unit and building purchase and sale transactions. This attorney manages the full range of legal issues that arise in running a building, including governing document work, vendor contracts, and day-to-day compliance questions. This role is ideal for a transactional real estate attorney seeking a boutique environment where they can deepen a specialized practice, build lasting client relationships, and grow alongside a collaborative, entrepreneurial firm.

What You’ll Do

• Manage purchase and sale transactions involving cooperative and condominium units and buildings, from contract through closing
• Draft and review proprietary leases, bylaws, and house rules, and assist boards in enforcing these governing documents
• Prepare AIA contracts and access license agreements, including negotiating access agreements (Article 881 experiences required)
• Advise board members and managing agents on day-to-day legal matters and regulatory issues affecting the building

• Draft materials for and provide legal guidance at board and shareholder/unit owner meetings
• Advise on budget and expense matters, including dispute resolution as needed
• Coordinate closings, ensuring documentation, logistics, and timing are accurate and handled with care
• Advise clients on applicable local, state, and federal compliance issues
• Support borrower-side financing and refinancing transactions

Individuals who share our core values

• Tenacious - Grit & perseverance when the going gets tough
• Pushing Boundaries - Creative approach to problem-solving
• Character Counts - Collaborative and collegial people, who take responsibility and maintain accountability & high emotional intelligence
• "Big Law" Approach - Intellectually curious, proactive, high standards

and also

• Bring relevant experience as a junior associate or associate attorney in a law firm, with specific experience supporting commercial real estate transactions.
• Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and appetite for learning, seeking a smaller, up-and-coming firm where they can have real impact and grow their skills.
• Value a high-caliber, collegial culture that is collaborative, responsive, and relationship-driven with colleagues and clients.
• Embrace technology (including legal tech and AI tools) and is eager to learn and adopt new systems that enhance efficiency and quality of work.
• Demonstrate strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple transactions simultaneously.
• Thrive in a fast-paced environment, taking pride in accuracy, professionalism, and supporting attorneys and clients effectively.

• Juris Doctor (J.D.) from an accredited law school and admission to practice in New York
• Approximately 4–7 years of relevant experience in transactional real estate, with a strong background representing or advising cooperative and condominium boards
• Demonstrated experience drafting and negotiating governing documents, vendor and contractor agreements, closing documents, and commercial leases
• Ability to act as transfer agent on behalf of cooperatives, as well as review and advise on stock and lease transfers
• Ability to advise on and facilitate Board meetings, meetings of shareholders and unit owners
• Strong research and writing skills, with a solid academic record
• Comfort advising boards and managing agents directly, translating complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, practical guidance
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the organizational skills to manage multiple matters and client relationships simultaneously
• Comfortable with technology, including legal tech and AI tools, and eager to adopt systems that improve efficiency and quality of work

Compensation & Benefits

• Health & Wellness Benefits – Substantial employer contributions toward comprehensive insurance, consistent with NYC legal market standards

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description:
This role will be based in Sunnyvale, San Francisco, or New York City. At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

Responsibilities:

AI is at the core of how LinkedIn connects more than a billion members to opportunity across jobs, sales, marketing, content, and trust platforms. As an AI Software Engineer you will own end-to-end machine learning systems that run in production at LinkedIn scale. You won't just train models, you will own the recommender and classification system that power LinkedIn’s core products. Your responsibilities cover the full product lifecycle from translating product requirements into system design, training the models to power the system, driving the experiments that prove efficacy, and managing the GPU fleets that run them at scale in milliseconds; you are the engine that drives value for our members.

This is an individual-contributor role; we expect you to be the owner of a well-defined significant workstream, align technical direction within your team, review code and technical designs from your team, and to deliver measurable member and business impact with a sense of urgency.

What success looks like in your first year

• Grow to the owner of an AI workstream end to end and ship at least one model-based system to a measured impact on member or business value.
• You become the go-to point of contact for your domain within our team and help others onboard to it as needed.
• Implement an efficiency or quality improvement (i.e. inference/training efficiency, engineer velocity, or tech-debt removal) backed by data.
• You operate systems reliably as on-call and work with senior engineers to root-cause at least one significant production regression.

Why LinkedIn

You'll work on AI systems with immediate, measurable impact on more than a billion members, alongside engineers who set the industry bar for recommendation systems at scale powered by the latest open source generative models and GPU inference. We encourage staying up to date on industry state-of-the-art and sharing your work with the community through conference, journal, and blog publications. We invest in your growth with real mentorship, we trust you with real ownership, and we measure what matters: impact, not output according to our core engineering principles.

• Impact: quantify the value you created for members, the business and your team
• Leadership: communicate and lead through influence, not authority
• Execution: deliver impact with a sense of urgency
• Craft: innovate and create leverage with high-quality solutions

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related technical field or equivalent technical experience
• 1+ years experience with machine learning, data mining, and information retrieval or natural language processing
• 1+ year of industry experience in software design, development, and algorithm related solutions.
• 1+ years experience in programming languages such as Java, Python, etc.

Preferred Qualifications

• 2+ years of relevant AI/Machine Learning experience.
• MS in Computer Science or related technical discipline
• Experience with PyTorch or similar Deep Learning frameworks
• Experience with Spark for data manipulation and transformation
• Experience with A/B testing at scale in a consumer-facing product
• Experience with AI code development (i.e ClaudeCode, Codex, Copilot)
• Experience adapting pre-trained LLMs to production systems including fine-tuning and student-teacher model paradigms
• Published work in academic conferences or industry circles.

Suggested Skills

• Data Mining
• Data Coding
• Machine Learning

You will Benefit from our Culture

Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor. jobs.description:

As a Coating Line Operator you will be assigned to work on a coating line and may work in one or more work stations including the face unwind, liner unwind, main console/winder, and PMA lab. You may be proficient on more than one coating asset in a given location. • Meet production schedules and program production sequences for optimal productivity.
• Follow standard operating procedures and specifications or instructions of higher level technical personnel and monitor meters, gauges, valves, flow ratios, temperatures, pressures, and related controls and guidelines to ensure adherence to production/process specifications.
• Maintain accurate production records and logs of equipment and product performance.
• Participate in group problem-solving teams and other continuous improvement activities. Support ELS initiatives to improve manufacturing performance (throughput, scrap reduction, safety, ISO work instructions, ELS
• Lead shift turnover discussions, communicate daily priorities to the team, and assist in keeping MDI boards up to date. Teamwork: Assist and support other team members in meeting department and site goals. Participate and share in performing all tasks necessary to run the facility. Contribute and participate in team decision making. Provide support in project work and other special requests. Train other employees on line tech responsibilities as requested.
• Accountable for daily production maintenance, preventative maintenance and housekeeping tasks according to established standards.
• Perform all other duties assigned by Supervisor.

Required:

• High school diploma or equivalent (GED) or 3+ years of relevant manufacturing work experience.
• Regard safety as a core value; must be willing and able to work safely; must always wear PPE.
• Demonstrate a strong quality and service focus.
• Good written and oral communication skills.
• Ability to read and comprehend documents related to product manufacturing.
• Able to work both individually and in a team-based environment.
• Able to work during the designated hours and accept a reasonable amount of overtime (including weekends).

• Demonstrate record of embracing and contributing to daily ELS processes and tools - MDI, standard work, 5S, etc.

jobs.title: Program Portfolio Analyst, PMO
jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position

The Product Portfolio Analyst is a core contributor on the Strategic Portfolio Management team, responsible for developing high-quality analyses, models, and visualizations that inform portfolio and resource allocation decisions. This role focuses on execution, analytical rigor, and insight generation, supporting senior PMO, and cross-functional leaders by translating data into clear, decision-ready outputs.

The Analyst works within established portfolio processes and frameworks, applies advanced analytical techniques, and partners closely with stakeholders to ensure data accuracy and analytical consistency across the portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio, Project Delivery & Resource Analysis

• Develop portfolio analyses to support strategic planning activities and drive decisions across product lines, business units, commercial regions and across the enterprise.
• Create frameworks, analyses, metrics and KPIs to yield insights in resource constraints, utilization, project execution and strategic alignment.
• Support scenario planning and tradeoff analyses across product programs, franchises indications, and platforms.

Data & Visualization

• Build high-quality dashboards, visualizations, and executive-ready materials that clearly communicate portfolio insights, risks, and assumptions.
• Ensure analytical outputs are accurate, well-documented, and aligned with portfolio data standards.

Tools & Process Support

• Support implementation, administration, and continuous improvement of Project Portfolio Management (PPM) tools and reporting processes.
• Partner with PMO and cross-functional teams to maintain portfolio data quality and consistency.

Collaboration & Communication

• Collaborate with PMO, R&D, Enabling Functions, Strategy, and Finance partners to understand analytical needs and deliver timely insights.
• Present analytical findings to managers and senior leaders, with guidance, in a clear and structured manner.

Required Skills & Experience

• 5+ years of relevant experience in product management, PMO, strategy, analytics, or a related field.
• Strong quantitative and analytical skills, with demonstrated ability to translate data into insights.
• Advanced proficiency in Excel, Smartsheet, data modeling, and visualization tools; experience with Snowflake and Tableau strongly preferred.
• Strong attention to detail and ability to apply structure to complex or ambiguous problems.
• Effective written, verbal communication and visual story-telling skills.
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple analyses and deadlines concurrently.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Engineering, or related discipline (required).
• MBA or advanced degree (preferred).
• MedTech or regulated industry experience (preferred).
• Experience with SQL, AI-enabled analytics, or decision analysis tools (e.g., DPL, Analytica) a plus.

Working Conditions

jobs.description:
A Residential Coordinator (RC), House Lead, or Lead DSP is a pivotal position in our homes! The RC is responsible for coordinating a variety of services including but not limited to; individual finances, community integration, program implementation, family involvement, and education/vocational programs. The RC is required to assist the Program Director in maintaining consistency in programming, individual care, and communication with staff and interdisciplinary team members.

• Assist the Program Director in maintain consistency within the program
• Coordinate individual finances

jobs.title: Creative Producer
jobs.description:
The Creative Producer is responsible for end-to-end production of all HTP visual and audio content, from capturing studio and field footage to final editing and podcast production. In this role, you will maintain high-quality creative standards across all marketing campaigns, donor communications, and events by executing video, audio, and graphic design work that aligns with brand standards.

Key responsibilities of the Creative Producer include but are not limited to:

• Plan, set up, and shoot high-quality video in studio and on location, managing lighting and sound and troubleshooting any audio and video issues in real time
• Edit footage into polished pieces for campaigns, social media, events, and donor communications
• Record, edit, and produce professional podcast episodes and other audio content, managing audio quality, lighting, and technical troubleshooting so the on air talent can focus solely on content
• Produce and adapt graphic design assets for print and digital formats using established templates
• Support occasional website content updates related to creative assets, campaigns, events, and donor communications
• Manage the full creative workflow from pre-production through final export and delivery
• Maintain the creative software stack, media storage, file naming conventions, and asset libraries for video, audio, photography, and design
• Maintain visual consistency and quality control across all output, ensuring adherence to brand guidelines
• Collaborate with field teams to gather content, and coordinate timelines with project managers and vendors
• Assist in the procurement and management of creative resources, including budget tracking for production projects and coordination with external vendors or contractors
• Work alongside the Project Manager to communicate production status and timelines to stakeholders

Applicants should be prepared to provide a portfolio or work samples that demonstrate video production, editing, audio production, and design execution. Additionally, the following qualifications must be met:

• Affirms and aligns with Help The Persecuted's Statement of Faith
• 3–5 years of experience in video production, with editing as a core strength
• Proficiency with professional video and audio equipment and editing software like Adobe Premiere, After Effects, and Audition
• Experience producing and editing podcast or long-form audio content
• Working graphic design skills, with the ability to execute from templates (Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or comparable tools)
• Experience managing media storage, asset libraries, and creative file workflows
• Strong creative eye and attention to detail
• Ability to manage multiple projects and deliver on deadline
• Willingness to learn and adopt emerging technologies, including AI assisted video and audio tools, in ways that remain authentic and do not misrepresent the people or stories being told
• Familiarity with brand systems and asset management

Preferred Experience

• Strong graphic design background beyond template work
• Experience capturing stories in the field or in sensitive environments while protecting the dignity, safety, and privacy of those being represented
• Motion graphics and animation experience
• Experience in nonprofit or faith-based environments

Success Profile

This role is ideal for someone who:

• Loves the craft of production and takes pride in finished work
• Can carry a piece from concept through final delivery
• Is comfortable across video, audio, and design rather than specialized in only one
• Works well on tight timelines without sacrificing quality
• Is detail-oriented and takes ownership of outcomes

Desired Characteristics of Applicants

When Help The Persecuted reviews applicants for an open position, we look for certain characteristics we believe are important to maximizing the ministry of HTP and fully utilizing the spiritual gifts and talents as individuals.

• Christian. We believe that to contribute to our mission it is essential that a person maintain a vibrant Christian faith.
• Called. Work at HTP is not just another job; it is the work of God and an employee should sense the call of God on his or her life work within the ministry.
• Competent. In addition to being a Christian and having a sense of calling, a person must be fully competent to perform all the duties of the position.
• Committed. Because of HTP’s high standards and its belief in good stewardship, it is essential that all employees manifest a high level of commitment to their job responsibilities and the ministry as a whole.

Work Environment

• This is a hybrid role based in Marietta, GA
• Team members are expected to work in the office 3 days per week
• Up to 2 days per week may be worked remotely
• Occasional travel may be required for field or event capture

Compensation and Benefits:

• Salary
• 403(b) retirement plan with matching contribution (following one year in the plan)
• Paid medical and dental; optional vision available
• Paid vacation, holiday and sick time

Help The Persecuted (HTP) is both an equal-opportunity employer and a Christian, nonprofit, religious organization. We conduct hiring without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, age, sex, marital status, parental status, or disability of an otherwise-qualified individual. The status of HTP as an equal-opportunity employer does not prevent the organization from hiring staff based on their religious beliefs so that all staff share the same religious commitment, which is central to our stated religious purpose and day-to-day operations.

jobs.title: Senior Cost Manager / Quantity Surveyor - Life Sciences Construction
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is seeking an experienced Senior Cost Manager and/or Quantity Surveyor to serve as a key day-to-day client interface, ensuring client objectives are achieved through the delivery of high-quality cost management services. This role will support the delivery of major capital construction projects, including large-scale manufacturing and advanced technology facilities, from planning and design through construction and closeout.

To be successful in this role, you must possess strong communication and stakeholder management skills and be comfortable operating in a client-facing environment. The ideal candidate will be self-motivated, driven, and capable of working independently while collaborating effectively within a project team. In this position, you will provide leadership and direction while promoting the purpose, values, and vision of Turner & Townsend.

Responsibilities:

• Estimating and negotiating change orders throughout the construction lifecycle.
• Provide estimate and cost planning to include producing and presenting the final cost plan.
• Review and participate with the design services team and general contractor in the development of cost estimates.
• Reconcile changes and assist the general contractor to ensure that their data is accurate.
• Communicate or meet with the general contractor and owner or project manager to gather status information to prepare a cost estimate update.
• Prepare written comments to the general contractor’s submissions, including the executive summary.
• Coordinate all sources of cost information for cost discussions and suppliers direct from NPA, subs, quantities from A/Es.
• Inform and drive engineering priorities based on cost impact.
• Work proactively with minimal supervision to resolve scheduling issues.
• Manage cost checks and carry out valuations on larger projects. Complete timely, accurate cost checking and valuation processes.
• Participate effectively with post-contract cost variances and change control processes.
• Manage cost impact, contingency management, and commitment tracking logs.
• Prepare funding data presentations and coordinate value engineering sessions with stakeholders.
• Develop cost plans and estimates through the design phase, delivering updated cost plans at appropriate design milestones.
• Provide commercial input to design optioneering and value engineering exercises.
• Review contractor and subcontractor pricing and lead negotiations on behalf of the client to achieve fair and competitive contract pricing.
• Perform quantity surveying, cost controls, and change management activities throughout the project lifecycle.
• Ensure that post-contract cost variances and change control processes are managed effectively.
• Ensure that cost auditing and valuation work is managed effectively and that a robust process for cost validation is in place.
• Carry out the production of monthly cost reports for presentation to the client.
• Ensure that final accounts are negotiated and agreed upon in a timely manner.
• Compile built cost estimate records for benchmarking purposes.
• Identify, coach, and mentor talent to realize their potential and celebrate the success of others.
• Display excellence in leadership and service delivery on commissions in line with the conditions of appointment.
• Financial Management: Utilize internal software to track ongoing margin levels and monthly fee/resource forecasts for each commission and financial reports.
• Implement and maintain the use of internal Business Management Systems and company delivery methodologies and tools to ensure consistent delivery of best practices for clients and the company.
• Be a role model who drives a one-business culture that achieves great outcomes for people, clients, stakeholders, and society.
• SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role and are to be adhered to where applicable.

• Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Cost Management, Quantity Surveying, Engineering, or a related construction field.
• A minimum of 7 years of relevant experience within the construction industry.
• RICS accredited or working toward accreditation preferred.
• Experience leading cost management on medium to large construction projects of moderate to high complexity.
• Experience supporting large-scale manufacturing, life sciences, technology, industrial, or commercial construction projects is preferred.
• Construction consultancy experience is strongly preferred.
• Strong understanding of construction industry technical matters, including procurement routes, value management, and value engineering.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to thrive in a client-facing environment while managing multiple priorities and project stakeholders.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs.*

The base salary range for this role is $120,000-$150,000 USD. This range reflects the company's good faith estimate of the base salary for this position at the time of the posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity. In addition to base salary, employees may be eligible for bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.title: Direct Support Professional / Caregiver
jobs.description:
What You Get to Do:

The Direct Support Professional (DSP) is responsible for providing direct support, hands-on instruction, assistance, and positive direction to individuals with intellectual/developmental disabilities (I/DD) in a manner that ensures their health, safety, successful achievement of service objectives, and personal goals.

jobs.title: Engineering Data Analyst
jobs.description:
AMS is seeking an Engineering Data Analyst to support the analysis of instrumentation data collected from operating nuclear power plants as part of AMS’s Online Monitoring (OLM) program.

OLM is a condition-based maintenance technology used to evaluate the performance, reliability, and long-term health of critical plant instrumentation. Rather than relying solely on periodic manual calibrations, OLM uses sensor measurement data and engineering analysis to determine whether instruments are performing within established limits and whether calibration or maintenance may be needed.

This is an applied engineering and data analysis role for someone who wants to work with real nuclear plant data, proprietary engineering software, instrumentation systems, and technically rigorous reporting. The Engineering Data Analyst will analyze plant operating data, support engineering evaluations, participate in field data acquisition activities, and contribute to reports used by nuclear utilities to make maintenance and calibration decisions by directly contributing to plant safety, reliability, and cost reductions.

Successful Engineering Data Analyst combine strong analytical ability with curiosity, sound judgment, attention to detail, and a commitment to quality. Training will be provided in AMS’s OLM methodology, proprietary analysis software, nuclear plant instrumentation, nuclear safety culture, nuclear plant work management and licensing strategies, quality assurance processes, and technical reporting requirements.

The goal of this position is to develop an engineer who can grow into a trusted technical contributor capable of independently performing OLM analysis, supporting field testing, preparing high-quality engineering reports, and helping advance and grow AMS’s condition-based maintenance technologies throughout the industry.

What You’ll Do

• Analyze sensor measurement data from operating nuclear power plants to evaluate the performance and condition of pressure, level, and flow instrumentation.
• Apply AMS’s OLM methodology to plant startup, steady-state, and shutdown data.
• Use proprietary AMS software tools to organize, process, analyze, and review plant instrumentation data.
• Identify trends, anomalies, data gaps, unusual instrument behavior, and potential instrumentation issues that require further technical evaluation.
• Prepare draft OLM mid-cycle and end-of-cycle reports documenting analysis results, conclusions, and recommended actions.
• Support the preparation of technical information for OLM amenability evaluations, limits reports, drift analyses, noise analyses, and related licensing documentation.
• Review transmitter definitions, plant data, supporting documentation, and analysis inputs for completeness, consistency, and technical accuracy.
• Participate in on-site data acquisition and testing activities at nuclear power plants and customer facilities as needed.
• Assist with plant-trip preparation, including pre-trip research, equipment configuration, documentation, checkout, and verification.
• Support field testing teams by acquiring data, documenting testing activities, performing preliminary analysis, and helping prepare customer deliverables.
• Complete plant-trip and laboratory documentation, internal trip reports, analysis notebooks, and quality assurance records.
• Support quality assurance testing of OLM-related software by executing test plans, documenting results, and reporting discrepancies.
• Learn and apply applicable nuclear industry standards, regulatory requirements, customer requirements, AMS procedures, and quality assurance processes.
• Work closely with senior engineers and technical leaders to resolve analysis questions and ensure results are accurate, defensible, and clearly communicated.
• Contribute ideas that improve AMS’s OLM analysis methods, software tools, procedures, reporting processes, and overall service quality.

These responsibilities reflect the core expectations established for AMS’s entry-level Engineering Data Analyst position, including OLM analysis, software proficiency, report preparation, quality assurance support, plant-trip participation, and disciplined documentation.

Who We’re Looking For

• A curious and analytical engineer who enjoys working with data, instrumentation, software, and real-world engineering problems.
• A detail-oriented professional who understands that small errors in data analysis or documentation can matter in a safety-critical industry.
• A critical thinker who looks beyond simply completing an analysis but asks whether the results are technically reasonable.
• A proactive learner who wants to master specialized engineering methodologies, proprietary tools, nuclear plant systems, regulatory expectations, and grow in their career at AMS.
• A clear communicator who can explain technical results, raise questions promptly, and represent AMS professionally with customers and plant personnel.
• A reliable and personally accountable team member who follows through on assigned work and takes ownership of results.
• A coachable engineer who accepts technical review and feedback as part of producing accurate, high-quality work.
• A collaborative professional who works effectively with engineers, technicians, managers, software developers, and customers.
• Someone who wants to build a long-term technical career in data analysis, instrumentation monitoring, condition-based maintenance, and the nuclear power industry.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Nuclear Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Data Science, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, or a closely related technical discipline.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work with numerical data, engineering software, spreadsheets, technical documentation, and structured analysis processes.
• Strong attention to detail in data review, analysis, documentation, and report preparation.
• Ability to follow established engineering procedures and work within a quality-assured environment.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet established project and report deadlines.
• Willingness to travel to nuclear power plants and customer facilities as needed.
• Prior experience with OLM is not required; training will be provided.
• U.S. citizenship is required due to contractual, regulatory, and nuclear facility access requirements.

Compensation & Benefits

• Health Coverage – Generous employer contributions toward comprehensive health, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
• Retirement – 401(k) with generous employer matching contributions
• Paid Time Off – 20 days annual vacation plus at least 10 paid holidays per year
• Professional Development – AMS is committed to your growth as a technical specialist; mentorship by senior engineers and PhDs, access to professional conferences, and continuing education opportunities in nuclear engineering and advanced analysis
• Career Growth – Annual salary reviews, raises, and advancement opportunities within a fast-paced, team-oriented, mission-driven organization
• Meaningful Work – The opportunity to perform engineering analysis that directly supports nuclear plant safety, reliability, maintenance optimization, and regulatory compliance.

Successful engineers at AMS combine strong technical aptitude with curiosity, sound judgment, attention to detail, and a commitment to quality. Training will be provided in AMS methodologies, proprietary systems, testing standards, nuclear industry expectations, and quality assurance processes.

The goal of this position is to develop an electrical engineer who can grow into a trusted technical contributor capable of supporting AMS’s core engineering and testing services with professionalism, accuracy, and accountability.

What You’ll Do

• Analyze real-world plant data, laboratory measurements, and electrical test results.
• Support testing and troubleshooting of instrumentation and control systems used in nuclear power plants.
• Assist with data acquisition, signal measurement, equipment setup, and analysis for commercial testing services, research projects, and engineering evaluations.

• Learn and apply applicable industry standards, test methods, customer requirements, and AMS procedures.

Who We’re Looking For

• A curious and proactive learner who wants to master new technical areas, tools, standards, and test methods.
• A hands-on engineer who enjoys working with equipment, measurements, software, data, and real-world systems.
• A detail-oriented professional who understands that documentation accuracy matters in safety-critical applications.
• A critical thinker with a practical problem-solving mindset and the judgment to ask good questions when needed.
• A clear communicator who can represent AMS professionally with internal teams, customers, and plant personnel.
• A reliable and personally accountable team member who follows through on assigned work and takes ownership of results.
• A collaborative engineer who works effectively with technicians, engineers, managers, and customers in a respectful, high-performing environment.
• Someone who wants to build a long-term technical career in a specialized engineering company serving the nuclear industry.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related technical discipline
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
• Interest in hands-on testing, instrumentation, controls, electrical systems, data acquisition, hardware, or applied engineering
• Ability to follow structured engineering procedures and work within a quality-assured environment
• Strong attention to detail in technical documentation, data analysis, test planning, and report preparation
• Clear written and verbal communication skills
• Willingness to travel to customer facilities and nuclear plants as needed

This position involves work under U.S. Department of Energy contracts and requires access to nuclear facilities. As a result, U.S. citizenship is required to meet federal compliance and security-access regulations.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience or coursework related to instrumentation and controls, circuits, signal processing, electrical measurements, data acquisition, power systems, controls, or hardware development.
• Experience with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, signal generators, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, data acquisition systems, or similar measurement tools.
• Exposure to laboratory testing, field testing, systems integration, nuclear power, aerospace, defense, automotive, manufacturing, or other regulated technical environments.

• Familiarity with EMC testing, EMI/RFI troubleshooting, or related standards such as MIL-STD-461 or IEC 61000 is a plus, but not required.
• Experience writing technical reports, test procedures, engineering evaluations, or structured documentation.

Compensation & Benefits

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager-Disaster Recovery
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a Senior Project Manager to support Emergency Assessment and Repair services for a federal client on the island of Kauai, Hawaii. In this critical leadership role, the Project Manager will oversee the rapid assessment, planning, coordination, and execution of facility and infrastructure repairs following natural disasters, severe weather events, and other emergency situations. The successful candidate will serve as the primary interface with the client, lead multidisciplinary teams, manage subcontractors, and ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and in compliance with federal requirements. This position requires strong program management, construction management, and stakeholder engagement experience related to federal clients.

This role will require an onsite presence in Kauai, Hawaii and is eligible for per diem related expenses when appropriate.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead emergency assessment and repair projects involving facilities, utilities, infrastructure, and mission-critical assets.
• Manage all phases of multiple projects from initial damage assessment and scope development through design, construction, closeout, and reporting.
• Coordinate rapid response activities following natural disasters and emergency events to support mission continuity and facility restoration.
• Review technical documents, repair plans, cost estimates, schedules, and construction submittals for quality and compliance with contract requirements.
• Monitor project performance related to scope, budget, schedule, quality, and safety objectives.
• Serve as the primary liaison between client representatives, contractors, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
• Oversee construction management activities, including field inspections, progress tracking, schedule reviews, and risk management.
• Manage and coordinate AECOM staff, subcontractors, and specialty consultants supporting emergency response and recovery efforts.
• Assist with project budgeting, invoicing, forecasting, construction accounting, and contract administration activities.
• Prepare and deliver project briefings, status reports, and presentations to senior leadership and stakeholders.
• Ensure project documentation, records management, and reporting requirements are maintained in accordance with federal and client standards.
• Support strategic planning efforts related to facility resilience, emergency preparedness, and long-term infrastructure recovery initiatives.

Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree and 8 years of relevant experience managing construction, infrastructure, facilities, emergency response, disaster recovery or related programs or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
• Ability to obtain and maintain access to secure federal facilities as required.
• A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
• US citizenship required.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Building Construction, or a related discipline.
• 20 years of professional experience managing emergency assessment, facilities restoration, infrastructure rehabilitation, construction, or federal programs.
• Five (5) years of experience on federal projects.
• Experience supporting federal programs.
• Experience managing large, complex task order contracts with federal agencies.
• Demonstrated experience leading disaster recovery, emergency response, facility repair, or infrastructure restoration efforts.
• Experience managing multidisciplinary teams in geographically remote or island environments.
• USACE Construction Quality Management (CQM) certification.
• Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Construction Manager (CCM), or similar industry-recognized certification.

Additional Information

• Position may require periodic travel throughout Kauai and to other Hawaiian Islands in support of program requirements.
