If you like a full pipeline, a fast sales cycle, and the satisfaction of closing deal after deal rather than waiting months on one, this is your kind of role.

Role overview

As a Commercial Account Executive, you'll bring Poka's connected worker platform to growing manufacturers across North America - running a high volume of deals end-to-end, from the first conversation through to close. You'll work smaller, faster-moving accounts than our Enterprise team, which means more at-bats, quicker cycles, and a real chance to build a track record fast.

You'll own your pipeline and your number: prospecting into the right accounts, running sharp discovery, building the business case, and closing with confidence. You'll do it alongside Sales Development, Solutions Consulting, Customer Success, and our IFS partners, with plenty of room to grow into larger patches as you prove yourself.

This is a great fit for someone with a couple of years of new business closing experience who wants to sharpen their craft in a fast-paced environment, with a real path to Enterprise or Strategic as they grow.

What you'll be doing

• Build and manage a high-volume pipeline through outbound prospecting, market research, and close collaboration with the Sales Development team

• Own the full sales cycle - discovery and needs analysis, product demonstrations, proposals, negotiation and close - moving deals at pace

• Build clear, tailored business cases that connect Poka's platform to each prospect's operational priorities

• Partner closely with Customer Success and cross-functional teams so customers move smoothly from signature to long-term value

• Keep opportunity tracking, forecasting, and account activity accurate and current in Salesforce

• Put AI to work in your day-to-day, research and account planning, conversation intelligence, drafting and CRM copilots, to sell smarter and spend more time with customers

• Bring customer insights and market feedback to leadership to help shape go-to-market strategy and product direction

• Contribute to lead generation initiatives and campaigns, drawing on your customer knowledge and industry trends

• Represent Poka at trade shows, industry events, networking opportunities, and virtual conferences

What you bring

• 3+ years of experience in B2B sales or a comparable Account Executive/closing role, with a track record of hitting or beating targets

• Experience selling SaaS, or strong transferable sales skills and a genuine interest in manufacturing or industrial technology

• Confidence running a full sales cycle independently and managing a busy pipeline

• Strong communication, negotiation and relationship-building skills

• A results-driven mindset and real hustle - you're motivated by volume and velocity, not just one big deal

• A hands-on, curious approach to AI and modern sales tooling - you already use it to work smarter and are keen to keep learning

• Excellent written and spoken communication and presentation skills in English

• Based in Central or East of the US, with great transport links and the ability and willingness to travel

We know great sellers come from varied paths. If you don't tick every box but you've got the drive and the numbers to back it up, we'd love to hear from you.

Why Poka

Manufacturers are under pressure to capture the knowledge of a retiring workforce, onboard new people faster, and get AI onto the floor in a way operators actually use, and Poka is one of very few platforms that does all three, already trusted at 3,000+ sites. You'll sell with the reach of IFS behind you and the pace and ownership of a growth-stage company, with a clear runway to grow your career as Poka grows across North America.

#LI-TK

What we offer:

• Scale-up energy with huge backing and a global yet close-knit team.

• Generous vacation policy, additional paid days, and charity day.

• Hybrid work policy - Employees who live within a 40 km radius of our Québec City office or a 15 km radius of our Montréal office are required to work in-office two days per week.

• 100% remote work if you do not live within the radiuses mentioned above.

• A truly flexible schedule that allows you to adapt your work hours.

• Group insurance from day one (dental, medication, disability, travel, etc.) with employer contributions, including access to telemedicine and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• A retirement savings plan with employer contributions.

• A MacBook Pro and a $500 home office allowance upon hiring.

• A generous annual learning and development budget to support your growth, plus the tools and opportunities you need to keep progressing in your career.

• A rewarding employee referral program for successful hires.

• Tasty snacks available at all times in our offices (fresh fruits, snacks, pastries, coffee, tea, etc.)

*Certain benefits are exclusively accessible to employees in Canada.

Want to learn more about our culture? Click HERE.

Please note: An understanding of English is essential at Poka, as it is the language used during company-wide meetings and many internal communications, ensuring effective collaboration and decision-making. In addition, as Poka operates in an international environment, English is the primary language for communicating with our clients and partners, enabling us to better serve them and represent Poka in a professional manner.

jobs.title: Manager, Events & Logistics
jobs.description:
WHAT IS THE ROLE

You are the marketing and logistics engine behind the External Engagement team's national footprint, and a key partner to the Senior Director of Programs in delivering the National Charter Schools Conference (NCSC). Reporting to the Chief of External Engagement, you turn strategy into flawlessly executed events and calls: Partner Fly-Ins, Congress on Campus visits, earmark technical assistance sessions, the State Leader Council's three annual convenings, APCSA convenings, the team's recurring calls, and a significant supporting role on NCSC itself.

You work closely with the Senior Directors of External Engagement: Legal & Congressional Engagement and External Engagement: Partners, State & School Leaders, translating their program and content strategy into registration, scheduling, materials, promotion, and on-the-ground logistics. You also work closely with the Senior Director of Programs on NCSC, taking on real ownership of conference marketing — in close collaboration with the Communications team — and additional logistics and operational duties that help ensure the conference comes off without a hitch.

Operating across a demanding, overlapping calendar of political travel, convenings, and the organization's flagship annual conference, this role requires exceptional organization, comfort with logistics under pressure, and a marketer's instinct for driving attendance and engagement.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Run Event and Convening Logistics

• Plan and execute logistics for Partner Fly-Ins (NCSW, NSCW), Congress on Campus visits, and earmark TA sessions

• Plan and execute logistics for the three annual SLC convenings and APCSA convenings, including venue and vendor coordination, invitations, and materials

Coordinate Recurring Calls

• Schedule and staff the CMO monthly call, SLC monthly calls, and quarterly school and network leader calls

• Prepare agendas and briefing materials, and track action items to closure

Support NCSC Delivery

• Serve as the Senior Director of Programs' primary logistics and operations partner for NCSC, with a larger role in ensuring the conference is delivered smoothly

• Lead conference marketing and promotion in close collaboration with the Communications team, driving registration and session attendance

• Take on additional conference logistics and on-site operational duties as needed — vendor coordination, troubleshooting, and day-of execution — to support a seamless attendee experience

• Coordinate with the Programs team on the SLC convening and receptions that take place at NCSC

Market External Engagement Programming

• Promote fly-ins, convenings, webinars, and calls to drive strong registration and attendance

• Develop marketing materials and communications that support the team's recurring programming

WHO YOU ARE

Experience

• You bring 4–7 years of experience in event planning, meeting logistics, or program operations, ideally in a nonprofit, association, or political environment

• You have experience marketing or promoting events to a professional audience, ideally including a large-scale conference

• You have managed vendor and venue relationships and multi-city or multi-event logistics calendars

• You have experience collaborating with a Communications or Marketing team on a shared deliverable

Skills and Approach

• You are exceptionally organized and can run several concurrent events and calls without dropping details

• You have a marketer's eye for what drives registration and engagement, not just a planner's eye for logistics

• You are calm under pressure when travel, venues, or schedules change at the last minute

• You collaborate easily with senior leaders who own strategy while you own execution, and with partner teams like Communications who co-own a deliverable with you

This position requires regular travel for fly-ins, convenings, and NCSC.

WHAT WE OFFER

The National Alliance for Public Charter Schools offers a sector-leading salary and benefits package. We cover 100% of an employee's medical, dental, and vision premiums, and 50% for spouses and dependents, including an HRA to cover 100% of in-network medical deductibles. We also offer:

• 403(b) retirement account with up to a 6% match after 90 days of employment

• Automatic life insurance coverage, short- and long-term disability coverage, and FSA

• 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave

• 25 PTO days annually, plus every federal holiday and a week off at year-end

• Monthly reimbursement for internet and cellular service, plus a $500 home office setup stipend in your first 90 days

The anticipated starting salary range for this role is $60,000-$85,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

WHO WE ARE

The National Alliance for Public Charter Schools believes that all families deserve high-quality public school options. Charter schools are independent public schools providing families with a new set of public school options. Each of these schools is developed to be a partnership between parents, teachers, and students.

When given the option, parents are choosing to enroll their children in charter schools. In fact, the demand for charter schools is far outpacing the supply in most communities. What began as a small movement in a few states has grown to become a major force in education reform across the country. Through advocacy, research, and strategic communications, the National Alliance works to grow the number of high-quality charter schools available to all families, especially those who do not have access to high-quality public schools.

To apply, please visit: www.publiccharters.org/jobs

jobs.title: BCBA Clinical Quality Specialist
jobs.description:
ABOUT FINNI HEALTH

Finni Health helps BCBAs go independent. We provide the infrastructure they need to start, run, and grow their own autism practices — including credentialing, payer contracting, revenue cycle management, HR, compliance, and purpose-built software.

We work alongside practice owners so they can spend less time fighting the operational complexity of running a healthcare business and more time building great teams and delivering care.

We're a fast-growing company backed by Y Combinator and General Catalyst, supporting 70+ BCBA-led practices across 22+ states and continuing to expand.

We're building the infrastructure behind the next generation of autism care — and we're looking for people who want to help build it with us.




ROLE OVERVIEW

The Clinical Quality Specialist translates identified needs into training, resources, processes, and improvements that directly enhance the platform, provider skills, and uphold clinical quality across practices. This role starts by owning record reviews and audits (today largely manual), partners with Product and Engineering to automate and improve functions, and ensure that tools and workflows support clinicians and high-quality care. The role evolves into a project-driven clinical partner who supports clinical and clinical operations projects as they arise, with focuses such as onboarding & training, supervision, professional development, clinical quality, consultation, and continuous improvement alongside the Clinical Success Manager.

Your first assignment is maintaining and auditing our clinical record systems.

A clinical record that hasn't been reviewed is a compliance risk nobody's caught yet. Right now, record reviews and audits happen manually, and there's no system tracking what's been checked, what's missing, or where the gaps are. That's the gap this assignment closes.

Expect this to take about 3-6 months for completion. What we need built:

 - Manual record reviews, done reliably. Own the audit and record request process today while the automated version gets built underneath it.

 - A documented SOP. Understand the current process end to end and write it down: who does what, how a review actually gets completed, where it breaks.

 - Automation opportunities identified and pursued. Flag where the manual process can be systematized, and work with Product and Engineering to actually get it built.

 - An internal auditing dashboard. As pieces get automated, build the reporting that shows what's been reviewed, what's outstanding, and related needs. Consider how we merge email and direct message requests with those in the compliance summary.

30–50% of your time is this to start. The remaining time goes to clinical projects: developing new clinical resources, professional development and training, maintaining what's already in place, and filling gaps as they surface, chosen with the Clinical Success Manager based on what's needed most. As the audit process becomes more automated, that split shifts: this becomes less of your time, and clinical and clinical operations initiatives become more, eventually up to 90%.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Clinical Record Review & Auditing

 - Own record reviews and audit/record requests, manually at first.

 - Document the current process as a living SOP the team actually uses.

 - Identify where reviews can be automated and partner with Product/Engineering to build it.

 - Once automated, build and maintain an internal dashboard tracking review status and gaps.

2. Clinical Projects: Develop, Maintain, Fill Gaps

 - Work through an ongoing slate of clinical projects chosen with the Clinical Success Manager developing new resources and processes, maintaining existing ones, and closing gaps as they're identified.

 - Take a project from rough idea to fully in place: help shape the design, then own execution, rollout with practices, and continuous monitoring.

 - As audit work shrinks, this becomes the larger share of the role.

3. Product & Engineering Partnership

 - Serve as the clinical voice on automating the audit/record review process by translating the manual workflow into requirements, testing the build, and confirming it solves the problem.

 - Monitor clinician feedback on any tools built and feed it back to Product and Engineering.

 - Support the development of clinical functions in Mission Control and Orbit.


ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES AS THE ROLE EVOLVES

4. Clinical Support & Consultation

 - Partner with the Clinical Success Manager to support clinicians with treatment planning, complex cases, and clinical decision-making.

 - Identify recurring clinical support needs and turn them into training, resources, or process improvements.

5. Training & Professional Development

 - As audit work becomes automated, take on a growing share of training and development work: resources and training that support BCBA and RBT competency, and ongoing professional development.

 - Use quality and audit data to identify training priorities.

6. Clinical Quality & Continuous Improvement

 - Partner with Clinical Success and Practice Support to monitor clinical quality and drive improvement using audit data, dashboards, and clinician feedback.

 - Identify trends and gaps in documentation, treatment integrity, and clinical competency, and turn them into training or process fixes.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - First 30 days: You can explain the current record review/audit process end to end and have a plan for the SOP.

 - First 60 days: The SOP is written and in use. You've identified concrete automation opportunities and are working with Product/Engineering on the first one. You've picked up your first clinical project.

 - First 6 months: Manual review time is measurably down. Automation is in place for at least part of the process, and an internal dashboard shows review status. You're already spending meaningful time on clinical projects, support, and training work.

 - Beyond: The audit process runs largely on its own, monitored through the dashboard. Your time is now mostly supporting clinical and clinical operations initiatives.


ABOUT YOU

 - You are a BCBA with 5+ years of clinical experience, ideally including direct oversight of RBTs and clinical supervision of other BCBAs.

 - Communication and Collaboration: Excellent written and verbal communication across stakeholders, with proven ability to work across internal teams and with external stakeholders. Most of what this role produces is written and built so teams can actually use it.

 - Clinical Enablement & Systems Design: Proven ability to build training, resources, and frameworks tailored to Finni’s unique model. Because our practice owners hold clinical autonomy and are not our employees, you are not managing them; instead, you are empowering them. You will design the training, supports, and systems that help them maintain high clinical standards, regulatory compliance, and ethical practices.

 - Clinical Judgment: Strong grounding in clinical record standards, documentation, and quality. Comfortable both doing the manual review work and designing the system that replaces it.

 - Proficiency: Proficient in Clinical Standards, Google, Messaging systems, EHR, dashboard and data analysis.

 - Mission Alignment: Passion for the mission of supporting quality autism care and empowering independent providers to run strong, compliant, and ethically sound practices.

 - Adaptability and Agility: Thrives in a fast-paced, fluid environment where the frameworks and protocols haven't been fully written yet, because you are a contributor toward their development. You are comfortable owning a manual, unglamorous process today with the explicit goal of automating yourself out of it and growing into a broader clinical development role as that happens.


BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation

 - 401(k)

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - Flexible work schedule

 - Paid time off

 - Paid holidays

 - Opportunity to have a meaningful impact on the growth of a rapidly scaling healthcare company

 - Work directly with ABA providers and Finni leadership to shape the future of the provider experience

jobs.title: Senior Manager, GTM Systems Delivery
jobs.description:
At MNTN, we put our people first, full stop. This allows our company culture to be defined by our team members and their shared values, like trust, ambition, quality, radical honesty, and compassionate leadership. It’s why we all really love working for the Hardest Working Software in Television™ (and also why we were named one of Ad Age’s Best Places To Work in 2026.)

We pride ourselves on bringing unrivaled performance and simplicity to Connected TV advertising. Our self-serve technology makes running TV ads as easy as search and social, helping brands drive measurable conversions, revenue, site visits, and more. It’s what led MNTN to being named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies in 2023. You can learn more about us and everything we do by visiting https://mountain.com/.

We’re committed to innovation that empowers, not replaces. At MNTN, AI is a tool for growth, enhancing efficiency while keeping a people-first approach. Our goal is to streamline workflows and drive new solutions—without compromising the human element that makes our company great.

So if wanting to do more, own more, and make a bigger impact comes naturally to you, then you may be the person we're looking for to join us in our next stage of growth.

MNTN is looking for a Senior Manager, GTM Systems Delivery to lead the team delivering high-priority changes across Salesforce and our connected GTM technology stack. You’ll keep urgent initiatives moving without sacrificing the platform, integration, data, security, testing, and release standards that help our systems scale.

This is a technical people leadership role for someone who can guide solution design, develop a strong team, and stay close enough to the work to jump in when needed. You won’t be the primary builder, but you’ll bring the technical depth to evaluate solutions, challenge estimates, troubleshoot issues, and hold a high bar for quality.

You'll report to the Head of Revenue Operations & Systems and lead a multidisciplinary team spanning business analysis, Salesforce and business systems engineering, and systems enablement. You'll partner closely with the Salesforce Foundation team, RevOps domain leads, the Salesforce Architect, AI Engineering, Business Analytics Engineering, and Platform/Data Engineering.

What you’ll do

• Own the expedited GTM systems delivery lane from intake and scoping through solution design, build, testing, launch, enablement, and stabilization.

• Lead and develop a multidisciplinary systems team, setting clear ownership, performance expectations, technical standards, and growth plans. Step in to troubleshoot or build when critical work gets stuck.

• Turn executive and Revenue priorities into focused two-to-four-week delivery cycles with clear outcomes, scope, ownership, dependencies, technical direction, and definitions of done.

• Manage capacity across urgent initiatives, service requests, and planned work. Set service levels, surface tradeoffs early, and lead escalation conversations when demand exceeds capacity.

• Partner with RevOps leads, who own business priorities, process decisions, stakeholder relationships, and final acceptance, while your team owns solution design and delivery.

• Work with the Foundation team and Salesforce Architect to follow platform standards, limit unnecessary customization, and turn recurring issues into durable roadmap or technical-debt investments.

• Guide revenue-related AI requests to the right solution and coordinate data and reporting dependencies with AI Engineering, Business Analytics Engineering, and Platform/Data Engineering—without absorbing ownership that belongs with those teams.

• Use cycle time, aging, rework, deployment success, production defects, integration reliability, adoption, and stakeholder outcomes to improve how the team delivers.

What success looks like

• Independently own the expedited GTM systems portfolio, with clear intake, prioritization, capacity, scope, dependencies, risks, owners, and delivery plans.

• Establish clear roles, operating expectations, and development priorities for the Business Analysis, Systems Engineering, and Systems Enablement team.

• Lead at least one priority Salesforce or cross-system initiative through design, build, testing, release, and stabilization with clear business acceptance and no critical production issues.

• Establish an effective technical-review partnership with the Foundation team and Salesforce Architect so expedited work follows platform standards and recurring issues are routed into the appropriate roadmap.

• Build trust with the stakeholders involved in assigned initiatives through clear updates, early escalation of risks, and transparent scope, timing, and capacity tradeoffs.

What you’ll bring

• 7+ years of experience across Salesforce, Business Systems, GTM Technology, or enterprise applications, including 2+ years leading Salesforce, business systems, or multidisciplinary technical delivery teams.

• A current Salesforce Administrator or Platform App Builder certification, plus recent hands-on experience with Salesforce configuration and development. Platform Developer or architect-level experience is a strong plus.

• Experience leading high-priority, cross-functional work across Salesforce and connected GTM tools in a fast-moving Revenue organization.

• Strong technical knowledge of Salesforce Flow, data models, security and permissions, APIs, integrations, environments, testing, deployments, and common failure points across connected systems. You should also have a working knowledge of Apex and Lightning Web Components.

• A strong track record across intake, prioritization, capacity planning, requirements, UAT, release readiness, adoption, and post-launch stabilization.

• The ability to align senior leaders, translate technical constraints clearly, and keep scope, decisions, and ownership clear across cross-functional initiatives.

• Experience developing technical talent, delegating effectively, and creating accountability without becoming the team’s primary builder—along with sound judgment around urgency, scope, and platform tradeoffs.

Nice to have

• Experience applying product operations, Shape Up, or similar appetite-based planning methods to enterprise systems work.

• Experience with Salesforce delivery tools, Jira, source control, release management, and CI/CD practices.

• Familiarity with AI-assisted development and operations, agentic workflows, and governance for revenue-facing AI use cases.

About MNTN

Our recruiters will always reach out using an email address ending with @mountain.com OR @mntn.com. If you’re contacted by someone without that address and they mention a Reference Code (which we never use), then that ain’t us folks. Tell those trolls to take a hike–you’re waiting to climb a MNTN.

MNTN provides advertising software for brands to reach their audience across Connected TV, web, and mobile. MNTN Performance TV has redefined what it means to advertise on television, transforming Connected TV into a direct-response, performance marketing channel. Our web retargeting has been leveraged by thousands of top brands for over a decade, driving billions of dollars in revenue.

Our solutions give advertisers total transparency and complete control over their campaigns all with the fastest go-live in the industry. As a result, thousands of top brands have partnered with MNTN, including Tarte, Decked, and National University.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer
jobs.description:
What We Do

Wagmo is a modern pet healthcare company built around how pet parents actually care for their pets. We partner with employers to provide a complete approach to pet and pet-parent wellbeing, from preventive wellness plans and emergency coverage to 24/7 pet telehealth guidance. Our purpose is to unlock every pet parent's potential to provide extraordinary care, and we do it by bringing the same intentionality to pet benefits that the best employers bring to human healthcare. Founded in 2017 and female-founded, Wagmo is headquartered in New York City and trusted by leading employers nationwide.



What’s Important To Us

Our mission shapes everything we build and how we work together. We take fearless ownership of outcomes, collaborate with radical candor, and are always driven by the customers and pet parents who trust us. We think critically, follow through relentlessly, and find the extra 10% that turns good work into exceptional work. We keep it weird because the obvious answer is rarely the most interesting one. Our values aren't aspirational. We interview for them and hold each other accountable to them. If what you've read so far resonates with you and you want to be part of a team where every person makes the company meaningfully better, we'd love to hear from you..



About The Role

As Principal Engineer at Wagmo, you will be the named owner of our application architecture. Wagmo sells pet wellness and insurance directly to consumers and through employers, brokers, and benefits administrators. Over the past two years we moved our insurance program to a new carrier partner and built a provider-agnostic interface to make that possible. It works, and it is not finished: two generations of models still coexist behind feature flags, and the legacy path has to be supported for years. On the partner side, each new benefits administrator we onboard currently arrives as its own build, with its own file format, renewal cadence, and eligibility rules. Our growth depends on that stopping.

Architecture has been owned by the CTO to date. This role takes it over. You will set technical direction across insurance, claims, partner integration, and our AI systems, decide what we will not build, and leave designs that two squads can execute without escalating. You will do this with no direct reports, real influence, and your hands in the codebase.

The scope here is wide for our team, which is the appeal and also the challenge. There is no platform organization beneath you and no architecture review process to inherit beyond the one we started this year.



Our Tech Stack: React · Python · TypeScript · React Native · Kubernetes · Django · Next.js · Node.js · Flutter (legacy) · builder.io http://builder.io · GitHub · Slack · Notion · Claude

 

Core Responsibilities

 - Own the end state of Wagmo's insurance provider interface, including a documented retirement path for legacy provider models and the decision about when dual-write paths come out.

 - Design partner and carrier onboarding so that adding a new benefits administrator is a configuration exercise rather than an application build. File format, renewal cadence, group structure, and product eligibility should be configured, not coded.

 - Own architecture review: run it, hold decision rights in it, and maintain a decision log that the team can rely on. Success is squads unblocked without escalation.

 - Define a single identity architecture spanning enterprise SSO tenants, our partner portal, and consumer authentication, with per-tenant onboarding reduced to a documented, repeatable process that stands up to enterprise security diligence.

 - Own the architecture of our AI systems across claims adjudication, customer support, and internal engineering tooling: versioned prompts and strategies with a promotion path, controls that match their documentation, and a measured cost per automated decision.

 - Mentor squad tech leads and raise the standard of technical design across the team, without taking on people management.



What You’ll Need To Be Successful

 - Experience holding a cross-cutting architectural decision that touched several domains at once, and driving it from ambiguity to a shipped, documented outcome that other engineers built on. You should be able to name the option you rejected and the cost you knowingly accepted.

 - A track record of retiring and scaling systems, not just building them. You have lived inside a half-migrated codebase running two paths in parallel and know what it takes, organizationally as well as technically, to finish.

 - Depth in Python and Django, relational data modeling, and third-party integration at scale. Familiarity with Kubernetes and GCP is useful; you will not own the cluster.

 - Experience putting non-deterministic systems into production, with real opinions about evaluation, versioning, and who is allowed to change a model's behavior.

 - The judgment to say what not to build, and the written and verbal clarity to carry that argument with people who outrank you.

 - Comfort that "principal" here means unblocking two squads rather than presiding over ten. Experience in insurance, benefits, payments, healthcare, or another regulated, integration-heavy domain is a strong plus.



Why Consider This Role?

 - Pet spending in the U.S. has reached $200 billion and the category is still early in its lifecycle. Wagmo is building the platform to lead it. This role is the architecture of that platform, at the moment the decisions are still open.

 - Wagmo is a female-founded, Inc. 5000 recognized company where performance matters more than pedigree. We are growing fast, building something that matters, and there is real ownership equity in that journey.

 - The team is exceptionally smart, curious, and kind, led by transparent and low-ego leadership. We take the work seriously and never take ourselves too seriously. This is not a traditional 9-to-5 job. It asks for real dedication and impact, and gives you genuine flexibility and autonomy in return.



Key Benefits

 - Comprehensive health, vision, and dental coverage

 - HSA/FSA

 - 401(k) retirement planning with employer matching

 - Unlimited paid time off

 - Annual company holidays

 - Additional company-wide recharge days off

 - 12 weeks parental leave for eligible employees

 - Company paid Wagmo pet wellness and insurance plans

 - Regular company-wide events and team gatherings

 - Pet-friendly office

 - Catered lunches

jobs.title: Laborer/Utility Worker
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Utility Laborer is responsible for performing a variety of general labor and industrial cleaning duties in support of steel mill operations. This position assists with maintaining a safe, clean, and productive work environment through pressure washing, lubrication of equipment, material handling, scrap recovery, debris removal, shoveling, and other operational support activities. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to safety, reliability, and teamwork while working in a heavy industrial environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Perform industrial pressure washing of heavy mobile equipment, processing plants, roadways, and designated work areas.
• Conduct routine lubrication and greasing of mobile and stationary equipment as directed.
• Shovel material accumulations, slag, dust, scrap, and debris from operating and maintenance areas.
• Hand-pick scrap metal and recover reusable materials from designated work zones.
• Remove debris, trash, and other materials to maintain safe and orderly work areas.
• Perform general housekeeping duties throughout the facility, including sweeping, cleaning, and waste disposal.
• Assist maintenance and operations personnel with routine labor tasks.
• Follow all site safety procedures, lockout/tagout requirements, and environmental regulations.
• Conduct visual inspections of equipment and work areas and report unsafe conditions immediately.
• Utilize hand tools, shovels, brooms, pressure washers, grease equipment, and other tools safely and effectively.
• Support spill response and environmental cleanup activities as directed.
• Work safely around moving equipment, elevated temperatures, dust, noise, and other industrial hazards.
• Participate in safety meetings, training programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.
• Perform other duties as assigned by supervision.

• High School Diploma or GED preferred.
• Ability to pass a pre-employment background check and drug screen.
• Valid driver's license preferred.
• Ability to work safely in a heavy industrial or steel mill environment.
• Strong work ethic and dependable attendance.
• Ability to understand and follow verbal and written instructions.

Preferred

• Previous industrial, manufacturing, steel mill, construction, mining, or environmental services experience.
• Experience operating pressure washing equipment.
• Basic mechanical aptitude and lubrication experience.
• Experience performing industrial housekeeping or laborer duties.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to frequently lift, carry, push, and pull up to 50 pounds.
• Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, stoop, climb, and shovel for extended periods.
• Ability to work outdoors in all weather conditions.
• Ability to wear required PPE including hard hat, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, hearing protection, respirator, and other safety equipment as required.
• Ability to work around dust, noise, vibration, moving equipment, and high-temperature environments.

Work Environment

• Heavy industrial steel mill environment.
• Exposure to varying weather conditions, elevated temperatures, dust, noise, and mobile equipment traffic.
• Overtime, weekends, holidays, and shift work may be required based on operational needs.

This location requires membership in IUOE Local 542.  Employees have benefits through the union.

Harsco Environmental is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Disclaimer:

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not intended to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to this position.

jobs.title: Director of Client Success
jobs.description:
Director, Client Success

Client Success  |  Full-Time  |  Reports to VP/SVP, Client Success

Reports To

SVP, Client Success

Key Collaborators

Strategy & Analytics · Product · Operations · Commercial Leadership

Primary Focus

Retention · Expansion · Cross-sell

Ideal Background

Pharma patient services, sales training, or reimbursement hub experience




POSITION OVERVIEW




THE ROLE

PHIL is seeking a Director of Client Success who will serve as the primary strategic partner for a portfolio of pharmaceutical manufacturer clients. This is fundamentally a relationship and growth role — not an operational support role. The Director will own client retention, drive expansion (increasing the share of a client's prescriptions routed through PHIL versus other channels), and identify cross-sell opportunities across additional brands within client organizations.

The Director operates as the internal quarterback for every client engagement. While PHIL's Strategy/Analytics, Product, and Operations teams will regularly appear in client conversations as subject-matter experts, this role is responsible for orchestrating those interactions, ensuring continuity of the client relationship, and translating client priorities into coordinated action across PHIL's organization.

This role is the client's advocate inside PHIL and PHIL's most important voice in the client relationship. The Director must be equally credible with a VP of Market Access and a field sales trainer — and must be able to move fluidly between strategic conversations and operational follow-through.

 


CORE RESPONSIBILITIES




WHAT YOU WILL OWN




1.  RETENTION — DEEPENING CLIENT CONVICTION

Build and sustain deep, multi-level relationships across each client organization — from day-to-day program contacts through VP and SVP-level commercial and market access leadership. Ensure clients maintain strong conviction in the value PHIL delivers, with every engagement reinforcing that PHIL is a strategic partner, not a vendor.

 - Own the overall health and satisfaction of each assigned account; be the first to know when something is at risk and the first to act on it

 - Lead Quarterly Business Reviews end-to-end — coordinating PHIL's Strategy/Analytics and Product leads as SMEs, but owning the room, the commercial narrative, and the follow-through

 - Proactively identify and resolve issues before clients raise them; set the internal standard that no client should ever surface a problem PHIL didn't already know about

 - Build multi-level relationship maps for each account; actively expand relationships beyond the single point of contact to ensure executive visibility and stakeholder depth

 - Develop client advocates — individuals who will speak credibly about PHIL to peers and serve as references for new business




2.  EXPANSION — GROWING SCRIPT SHARE

Drive measurable expansion in each client's share of prescriptions routed through PHIL versus retail and other channels. Understand the commercial levers that move script share and work with clients' commercial and sales organizations to activate them.

 - Develop a deep understanding of each client's sales structure, territory model, and field team priorities — and build relationships with sales leadership and sales training teams to ensure PHIL is embedded in commercial execution

 - Translate program performance data into commercial narratives that resonate with brand and commercial leaders — framing insights in terms of net revenue impact, not just operational metrics

 - Work with Strategy/Analytics team to identify and recommend program optimizations (business rule changes, copay adjustments, affordability program design) that meaningfully improve pull-through rates and patient conversion

 - Track script share performance at the territory and HCP level; surface opportunity areas to the client's field team and sales leadership




3.  CROSS-SELL — IDENTIFYING NEW BRAND OPPORTUNITIES

Leverage deep relationships within existing client organizations to identify other pharma brands that would benefit from PHIL's platform. Act as an intelligent referral source for PHIL's commercial team.

 - Develop sufficient understanding of each client's portfolio to recognize brands that would benefit from PHIL's hub and pharmacy model

 - Build relationships with commercial leaders across multiple business units within each client organization — not just the teams managing current PHIL programs

 - Identify expansion signals (new launches, pipeline products, dissatisfaction with existing hub partners) and communicate them to PHIL's commercial team in a timely and structured way

 - Participate in new brand conversations alongside PHIL's commercial team, providing credibility through the existing relationship and institutional knowledge of the client




4.  INTERNAL QUARTERBACKING — ORCHESTRATING PHIL'S CROSS-FUNCTIONAL TEAM

Serve as the connective tissue across PHIL's internal teams — Strategy/Analytics, Product, and Operations — ensuring the client's priorities are understood and acted upon across the organization, and that the client experiences a seamless, coordinated partnership regardless of which PHIL team members they're engaging with.

 - Maintain a complete picture of each account: open priorities, ongoing initiatives, relationship dynamics, recent interactions across all PHIL functions, and upcoming decision points

 - Coordinate the participation of Strategy/Analytics, Product, and Operations leads in client engagements — briefing them on context, setting clear objectives for each interaction, and ensuring follow-through on commitments

 - Serve as the client's internal voice at PHIL: represent client priorities in product roadmap discussions, escalate operational issues with appropriate urgency, and advocate for investments that will improve client outcomes

 - Maintain clear accountability between internal teams — ensuring that client-facing commitments are tracked and that no action item falls through the gaps in a cross-functional handoff

 - Build and maintain an account plan for each client that is visible to all relevant internal stakeholders and updated regularly

 


WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE




18-MONTH SUCCESS PROFILE

A Director of Client Success who is performing at a high level at PHIL will be described by clients as a trusted advisor who understands their business, not just their program. Internally, they will be known as the person who always knows what's happening with their accounts and who makes cross-functional execution feel seamless.

 - Clients in their portfolio renew at a high rate and proactively expand their relationship with PHIL

 - Script share is measurably growing across their portfolio of accounts, with clear commercial narratives connecting PHIL's work to net revenue outcomes

 - They have identified at least one cross-sell opportunity per major client and have active conversations in progress with PHIL's commercial team

 - They have executive-level relationships at each client (VP/SVP Market Access, Commercial, or Patient Services) — not just day-to-day program contacts

 - They have built at least one identifiable advocate per account — someone who will take a peer call and speak credibly about PHIL

 - They are never the last to know about a problem with one of their accounts — they surface issues before clients raise them

 - Their clients' field teams and sales leadership view PHIL as a commercial partner, not a back-office function

 


QUALIFICATIONS




BACKGROUND & EXPERIENCE


IDEAL BACKGROUND (PRIMARY FIT)

The strongest candidates will have spent meaningful time inside a pharmaceutical company in a patient services, reimbursement, hub operations, or sales training capacity. This background produces a Director who understands the commercial pressures clients face, how field sales teams are structured and motivated, and what "great" looks like for a market access or hub program — not from the outside, but from having lived it.

 - 5+ years of experience within a pharmaceutical manufacturer in one or more of the following roles:

 - Patient services, patient access, or reimbursement program leadership

 - Hub or specialty pharmacy program management (manufacturer-side)

 - Sales training, field force effectiveness, or commercial operations

 - Market access, payer strategy, or value & access

 - Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally within a complex organization and influence without direct authority

 - Track record of building strong relationships with commercial and market access leadership




CLIENT SUCCESS / ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT EXPERIENCE (STRONG PLUS)

Prior experience in a client success, account management, or strategic partnerships role at a hub services company, specialty pharmacy, or healthcare technology company is a meaningful differentiator. Candidates with this background combined with pharma industry experience are strongly preferred.

 - Experience managing a portfolio of pharmaceutical manufacturer clients

 - Familiarity with hub services metrics: enrollment rates, pull-through/PTR, script share, GTN vs. retail, refill rates

 - Experience delivering QBRs and business reviews to VP/SVP-level stakeholders




SKILLS & CAPABILITIES (ALL CANDIDATES)

 - Exceptional relationship and communication skills — equally comfortable in a strategic conversation with a SVP and a working session with a field sales trainer

 - Commercially oriented — able to translate operational program data into net revenue narratives that resonate with brand and commercial leaders

 - Strong orchestration and project management instincts — comfortable coordinating multiple internal stakeholders on behalf of a client without letting anything fall through the cracks

 - Data-literate — able to read and interpret program performance data, identify meaningful patterns, and frame them as insights rather than just reporting

 - Executive presence and credibility — able to command a room at the VP/SVP level without losing approachability with day-to-day contacts

 - Proactive and anticipatory — wired to get ahead of problems, not react to them

 - Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in business, healthcare, or a related field is a plus

 


WHY PHIL




THE OPPORTUNITY

PHIL is redefining how pharmaceutical manufacturers connect patients to the therapies they need. Our digital hub and pharmacy platform is built to eliminate the friction in patient access — from enrollment and benefits verification through prior authorization, copay support, and dispensing — and to give manufacturers the commercial insight they need to drive better outcomes.

The Director of Client Success role sits at the center of PHIL's growth strategy. Peer referrals and trusted relationships are the primary driver of how pharmaceutical manufacturers select hub partners — which means every client relationship this Director builds and deepens is directly contributing to PHIL's ability to win new business. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role with direct exposure to PHIL's senior leadership and a clear path to growth as the company scales.

PHIL is at an inflection point in its growth. The Director of Client Success joining now will help define how we show up for clients as we scale — and will have an outsized influence on both PHIL's client experience and its commercial trajectory.




BENEFITS

Ground floor opportunity with one of the fastest-growing startups in health-tech

Fully remote working environment available in the following states: AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, IA, ID, IL, IN, MA, MI, MO, NC, NH, NJ, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, WV

Competitive compensation (commensurate with experience)

Full benefits (medical, dental, vision)

401(k) contribution opportunity



PHIL is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.description:
The Patient Care Technician reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Memorial, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Patient Care Technician’s primary function is to assist and support the Professional Registered Nurse in all aspects of direct and indirect patient care activities.  The Patient Care Technician functions as a member of the unit staff under the direction and supervision of the professional Registered Nurse.

Responsibilities:

• Direct Patient Care Activities Assists with admission, transfer, and discharge process.Takes and records temperature, pulse, respirations, weight for adults and/or neonates, height, and blood pressure.Measures and records intake and output including output from drains.Applies cardiac monitor/oximetry.Obtains EKG.Adheres to the infant security protocol (accurate assessment of band placement).Performs normal newborn hearing screening.Obtains capillary blood glucose for adults and/or neonates.Performs phlebotomy.Applies Fetal Monitor equipment on pregnant patients.Discontinues heplocks and foley catheters. Administers enemas.Collects specimens (urine, stool, blood and sputum) on adults and/or neonates. Makes rounds of patients and anticipates their needs and observes newborns in the nursery.Responds to patient call lights in a timely manner, especially emergency lights.Distributes fresh drinking water and nourishments to patients. Prepares patients for meals; assists or feeds patients as necessary. Feeds normal newborns as assigned.Provides morning care, bed baths and evening care according to established Nursing Care Procedures. Provides peri-care to appropriate patients.Provides newborn care to the infant including bath, dressing, obtaining foot prints, assistance with feeding (bottle and breast), glucose checks.Makes occupied and unoccupied beds.Ambulates patients and instructs on walker, cane and crutch walking as appropriate for assigned unit. Assists with pre-and post-operative care; positions patients as ordered; applies special equipment for safety; lifts and turns patients with proper and safe body mechanics and available resources.Applies comfort and safety measures (side rails and call lights). Sets up oxygen and suction equipment and other respiratory equipment for adults and/or neonates.Applies dressings to Stage I and Stage II skin breakdown. Prepares patient room for MD or RN assessment, evaluation, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Assists with procedures in the normal newborn nursery as directed.Transports patients, equipment and/or supplies during urgent and emergent situations and to front door on discharge.Responds to emergency situations, secures assistance and initiates basic life support.Reports observations and documents appropriately. Promptly notifies RN of any change in patient condition.Performs post-mortem care and transports bodies to the morgue when necessary.Assumes responsibility for the care of patient’s prosthetic devices, hearing aides, dentures, eye glasses, etc.Follows established policies, procedures and standards of care in all areas of practice.

• Indirect Patient CareMaintains a safe and clean environment. Duties may include: maintaining temperature logs on, defrosting, and cleaning refrigerator, straightening linen, cleaning utility rooms, cleaning IV poles, cleaning scale, cleaning and returning equipment to SPD, replacing and disposing of soiled linen bags.Performs duties delegated by the RN to facilitate patient care and the efficient operations of the assigned patient care unit.Collects and inventories patient belongings on admission, transfer and discharge.Completes charges using appropriate documentation.Orders supplies on-line or appropriate requisitions and stocks in appropriate location.Obtains necessary equipment and supplies to facilitate patient care.Assures room readiness for incoming patients.Checks designated equipment for proper functioning.Counts instruments and sterile trays sent and received from SEP as appropriate for assigned unit.Stocks and removes linen from patient rooms.Sets up and breaks down delivery table.Participates in staff meetings.Demonstrates cost effective approach to patient care in terms of equipment, supplies and other resource use.Participates in quality improvement activities.Participates in daily/weekly/monthly QC’s.Participates in orientation of new staff.Performs related duties as assigned.Uses established communication channels to resolve work related problems.Understands and consistently demonstrates principles of “Patient’s First” philosophy.Carries out assigned tasks and activities on a shift basis, as delegated by the RN.Assumes responsibility for meeting mandatory requirements.

• CPR recognition by the American Heart Association (BLS for Healthcare Providers).
• Minimum of 90% correct on annual mandatory Health and Safety Training quizzes.
• Unit based recognition for Capillary Blood Glucose Monitoring.

Preferred:

jobs.title: Director, External Engagement
jobs.description:
WHAT IS THE ROLE

You are the Senior Director's right hand across the Alliance's coalition, congressional, and state and school leader portfolio. Reporting to the Senior Director, External Engagement, you turn strategy into execution: drafting the materials, running the logistics, and tracking the follow-up that make the SCOTUS coalition, congressional programming, and state association and school leader engagement work land well and land on time.

While the Senior Director owns the strategy and the senior relationships with coalition leaders, Legal, and Federal Government Relations, you are the person who makes sure that strategy actually gets delivered: briefing materials are sharp, calls and convenings are well-prepared, partner letters go out on time, and field intelligence gets captured and turned into something useful.

Operating across several fast-moving workstreams at once, this role requires excellent judgment about what matters most this week, strong writing and drafting skills for varied audiences, and the discretion to work with sensitive legal and political information.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Support Coalition and Legal Strategy Execution

• Maintain coalition contact lists, meeting notes, and follow-up items for the SCOTUS coalition

• Draft briefing materials and talking points that translate legal and coalition strategy for partner and stakeholder audiences

• Coordinate scheduling and logistics for coalition convenings and calls

Support Congressional Programming Delivery

• Draft content and materials for Partner Fly-Ins, Congress on Campus visits, and earmark advocacy programming, in coordination with the Manager of Events & Logistics

• Support school and leader preparation ahead of Hill meetings, ensuring materials and messaging are ready for Federal Government Relations to use

• Help draft partner letters and track sign-on and targeting logistics

Support State Association and School Leader Engagement

• Prepare agendas, materials, and follow-up for State Leader Council (SLC) monthly calls and the three annual convenings

• Support CSA leader coaching logistics and track engagement across the 2028 implementation cohorts

• Prepare materials for quarterly school and network leader calls

Support Coalition Partner and Field Intelligence Work

• Help execute the playbook for soliciting partner and network-leader input on proposed rules and policy changes

• Compile field intelligence from coalition gatherings, focus groups, and 1:1 meetings into actionable reports

• Track coalition partner engagement and maintain accurate records in partnership with the Special Projects Coordinator

WHO YOU ARE

Experience

• You bring 7-10 years of experience in coalition politics, association management, policy or advocacy work, or program management

• You have experience supporting a senior leader or executive across complex, multi-workstream priorities

• You have experience drafting policy or advocacy materials for varied audiences — legal, congressional, and grassroots

• You have experience preparing materials and logistics for recurring calls or convenings

• You bring familiarity with charter schools, K–12 education policy, or state-level advocacy

Skills and Approach

• You are highly organized and comfortable managing several parallel workstreams without dropping details

• You are a strong, clear writer who can adapt tone and substance for legal, congressional, and grassroots audiences

• You exercise sound judgment and discretion with sensitive legal and political information

• You are comfortable operating a level below the primary strategy owner — proactive about execution without needing to hold every relationship yourself

• You anticipate what the Senior Director will need next and prepare for it before being asked

This position requires regular travel for SLC convenings, fly-ins, and NCSC.

WHAT WE OFFER

The National Alliance for Public Charter Schools offers a sector-leading salary and benefits package. We cover 100% of an employee's medical, dental, and vision premiums, and 50% for spouses and dependents, including an HRA to cover 100% of in-network medical deductibles. We also offer:

• 403(b) retirement account with up to a 6% match after 90 days of employment

• Automatic life insurance coverage, short- and long-term disability coverage, and FSA

• 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave

• 25 PTO days annually, plus every federal holiday and a week off at year-end

• Monthly reimbursement for internet and cellular service, plus a $500 home office setup stipend in your first 90 days

The anticipated starting salary range for this role is $85,000–$110,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

WHO WE ARE

The National Alliance for Public Charter Schools believes that all families deserve high-quality public school options. Charter schools are independent public schools providing families with a new set of public school options. Each of these schools is developed to be a partnership between parents, teachers, and students.

When given the option, parents are choosing to enroll their children in charter schools. In fact, the demand for charter schools is far outpacing the supply in most communities. What began as a small movement in a few states has grown to become a major force in education reform across the country. Through advocacy, research, and strategic communications, the National Alliance works to grow the number of high-quality charter schools available to all families, especially those who do not have access to high-quality public schools.

To apply, please visit: www.publiccharters.org/jobs

jobs.title: Software Engineer (Full Stack)
jobs.description:
About TensorWave

At TensorWave, we're revolutionizing AI computing by offering the most advanced cloud services, highlighted by our deployment of AMD Instinct Series GPUs. Our mission is to accelerate AI innovation by removing hardware limitations and ensuring scalable, efficient solutions for AI workloads. To support our rapid growth, we're seeking a Full Stack Engineer to join our team.



About The Role:

We are looking for a Full Stack Engineer to join our Product Engineering team. You'll build scalable, modern web applications and high-performance backend services that power TensorWave's next-generation AI cloud platform. Working directly with our cloud infrastructure team and UI/UX designers, you will lead the ground-up overhaul of our internal admin and customer-facing dashboards

This isn't a "close the ticket and move on" role. We're looking for problem solvers and owners who take full responsibility for what they build, dig into issues until they're truly solved, and consistently go above and beyond to deliver real value to our customers.



What You'll Do:

 - Lead the architecture and ground-up rebuild of our internal administrative tools and customer-facing dashboards.

 - Design and implement frontend applications using React.js and Next.js to provide seamless access to our GPU cloud services.

 - Develop robust APIs to support both multi-tenant cloud architectures and single-tenant, bare-metal deployments.

 - Develop and maintain GraphQL and REST APIs using Node.js, Express.js, and Apollo to handle complex data requirements.

 - Collaborate with the AI infrastructure team to integrate new GPU capabilities into our platform, utilizing Go (Golang) for high-throughput backend components.

 - Own features end to end, from design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.

 - Instrument services with OpenTelemetry and build dashboards in Grafana to monitor performance and drive proactive optimization.
   
   

Who You Are: 

 - An owner: You treat the product like it's yours and take accountability for outcomes, not just tickets.

 - A problem solver: You're energized by hard, ambiguous problems, and leverage first principles thinking to move the needle.

 - Customer-focused: You understand that the work matters because of the value it delivers to our users.

 - Proactive and self-driven: You are a T-shaped engineer who thrives in a lean startup environment; for you, stepping beyond the bounds of your role is second nature because you care deeply about solving hard problems and building resilient AI infrastructure at scale.
   
   

Essential Skills & Qualifications:

 - 5+ years of professional software development experience.

 - Strong proficiency in React.js, Next.js (including SSR), and modern frontend development.

 - Strong knowledge of GraphQL and the Apollo ecosystem (Client, Server, schema design).

jobs.title: Veterinary Assistant
jobs.description:
Who is VetEvolve?

VetEvolve is a network of veterinary practices built to support the people delivering care and the practices they lead. We combine clinical insight with operational strength to give our teams the support, tools, and structure they need to thrive, without losing what makes each practice unique. We are intentionally focused on growth, not as an end in itself, but as a way to strengthen our practices, expand access to care, and create more opportunities for our teams.

Guided by our values: Care First. Better Together. Grow Forward. Own It. We create an environment where veterinary professionals can do their best work, build meaningful careers, and deliver exceptional care. Growth with intention. Care without compromise.

Veterinary Assistant

🐾 Love Animals? Love Being Part of a Team? We Want to Meet You! 🐾

Are you the person who can’t walk past a puppy without saying hello, thinks cleaning up after pets is just part of the job, and genuinely enjoys making a difference in the lives of animals and their people? Then you might be exactly who we’re looking for!

Hollymead Veterinary Hospital is looking for an enthusiastic, compassionate Veterinary Assistant to join our team! If you’re dependable, eager to learn, enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, and want to be part of a team that truly cares about our patients, clients, and each other—we’d love to hear from you! 🐶🐱❤️

Position Summary:

The Veterinary Assistant provides essential support to the veterinarian during outpatient exams and throughout the diagnosis and treatment of patients. They care for all patients, assist with medical procedures, and help ensure each patient receives high-quality, compassionate care. In this role, the Veterinary Assistant also serves as a key connection between the veterinarian and clients. Through exceptional service and communication, the Veterinary Assistant helps build trust and foster lasting relationships with clients and their pets.

Primary Responsibilities:

• Provides compassionate, professional care to patients and clients at all times.

• Communicates clearly and respectfully with clients, doctors, and team members, including answering phones and routing inquiries as needed.

• Handles sensitive client situations with empathy and discretion, escalating medical questions appropriately.

• Assists the veterinarian during exams, diagnostics, treatments, and surgical procedures.

• Safely restrains animals of varying sizes and temperaments using low-stress handling techniques.

• Administers medications, draws up vaccines, collects lab samples, and performs basic lab tests as directed.

• Creates, reviews, and enters treatment plans accurately in the medical record system.

• Educates clients on common vaccinations, medications, and treatment protocols to ensure understanding of care plans and follow-up recommendations.

• Accurately records patient information and maintains organized, up-to-date medical records.

• Enters charges accurately and assists with the client check-out process, including processing payments when needed.

• Ensures exam rooms, treatment areas, and hospital spaces are clean, stocked, and well maintained.

• Demonstrates consistent reliability, punctuality, and commitment to supporting patients, clients, and hospital operations.

• Performs all other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

• High school diploma or equivalent required.

• Basic computer proficiency, including the ability to use practice management software and Microsoft Office applications.

• Previous experience working with animals preferred; veterinary or animal care background strongly valued.

• Able to work safely around cleaning chemicals, anesthetic gases, radiation, zoonotic diseases, and animal bodily fluids.

• Maintains composure and professionalism in emotionally challenging or high-stress situations.

• Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds and safely handle animals up to 130 pounds.

• Comfortable sitting, standing, walking, bending, and kneeling for extended periods throughout the workday.

• Professional, neat appearance consistent with hospital standards.

Hours:

• Must be able to work a flexible schedule and be available for scheduling during all hours the practice is open to support hospital operations.

Compensation and Benefits:

Compensation: $17-20/hour, commensurate with licensure and experience

• We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage. In addition, employees are eligible to participate in our 401(k) retirement plan. Other benefits include paid time off, paid holidays and access to employee assistance program.

Ready to Learn More?

We look forward to learning about your unique priorities and goals and working together with our local hospital teams to support you.

jobs.title: QA Analyst - Intermediate
jobs.description:
Ingram Marine Group is looking for a QA Analyst - Intermediate to join our team. This role independently performs software quality assurance activities for application development projects, system enhancements, integrations, and production releases. This position develops and executes comprehensive testing, manages defects, identifies quality risks, and contributes to test automation efforts that improve coverage, efficiency, repeatability, and release confidence. The role collaborates with Business Analysts, Application Developers, Product Owners, Project Managers, and business stakeholders to verify that technology solutions meet business and technical requirements. The role would encompass the below responsibilities.

• Independently plan and execute functional, integration, system, regression, user acceptance, API, performance, and post-deployment testing as appropriate.

• Develop and maintain comprehensive test plans, test cases, test scripts, test data, expected results, traceability, and supporting QA documentation.

• Analyze business requirements, technical specifications, user stories, process flows, and acceptance criteria for clarity, completeness, and testability.

• Identify, document, prioritize, track, and communicate software defects, testing issues, dependencies, and quality risks.

• Participate in or facilitate defect triage and collaborate with technical and business resources to support timely resolution.

• Coordinate test environments, test data, schedules, dependencies, and business participation for assigned efforts.

• Communicate testing status, results, unresolved defects, risks, and release-readiness observations to project stakeholders.

• Support release validation, production implementation, and post-deployment verification activities.

• Apply and promote established QA standards, processes, procedures, documentation templates, and best practices.

• Identify functional, integration, regression, API, and other repeatable tests that are appropriate candidates for automation.

• Design, implement, execute, and maintain automated tests using approved tools, frameworks, and standards.

• Partner with Application Developers and other technology resources to troubleshoot automated test failures and improve automation reliability and coverage.

• Incorporate automated tests into application delivery and continuous integration processes where appropriate.

• Monitor defect trends and testing results to identify opportunities for process and quality improvement.

• Participate in root-cause analysis of production defects and recommend preventive or corrective actions.

• Provide guidance and knowledge transfer to less experienced QA resources when requested.

• Serve as a knowledgeable QA resource for assigned applications, projects, or business processes.

Degree Required:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, Business, or a related field. An equivalent combination of relevant education and experience may be considered.

Years of Experience Required:

Three or more years of progressive experience in software quality assurance, software testing, business application testing, or a related technology role.

Certification Required:

Quality assurance, software testing, Agile, or test automation certifications are preferred but not required.

• Solid knowledge of software quality assurance principles, testing methodologies, processes, and best practices.

• Proficiency developing and executing test plans, test cases, test scripts, test data, traceability documentation, and testing reports.

• Experience performing functional, integration, system, regression, user acceptance, API, performance, and post-deployment testing as appropriate.

• Experience identifying automation candidates and developing, executing, and maintaining automated tests.

• Knowledge of automated testing tools, frameworks, scripting approaches, and continuous integration practices.

• Experience with defect tracking, test management, work management, and software development collaboration tools.

• Ability to analyze business and technical requirements and translate them into effective test scenarios.

• Ability to identify quality risks, dependencies, coverage gaps, and process improvement opportunities.

• Working knowledge of relational databases and queries used for data validation and testing.

• Working knowledge of application integrations, APIs, batch processes, interfaces, and data flows.

• Strong analytical, troubleshooting, critical-thinking, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to independently manage multiple assignments, priorities, and deadlines.

• Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, documentation, and collaboration skills.

• Ability to communicate defects, risks, status, and recommendations to technical and business audiences.

Working environment:

• • Standard office environment with the ability to sit at a workstation for extended periods. • Regular use of computers, software applications, testing tools, communication platforms, and other office technology. • May require extended or nonstandard working hours to support significant application releases, production implementations, or critical issue resolution. • May require coordination with technical teams, business stakeholders, vendors, or resources working in different locations or schedules. • Must be able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a collaborative, deadline-oriented environment.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

• A competitive compensation package
• Comprehensive benefits including Medical/Prescription Drug plans, HSA, Vision, Dental and Health Care FSA.
• Generous paid time off benefits
• 401K match upon first day of hire
• Life and AD&D, Employee Assistant programs, Group Legal, & more
• Associate growth and development encouraged through internal training and tuition reimbursement program

jobs.title: People Operations, Project Coordinator - COO Support, Senior Associate
jobs.description:
About TPG

TPG is a leading global alternative asset management firm, founded in San Francisco in 1992, with investment and operational teams around the world. TPG invests across a broadly diversified set of strategies, including private equity, impact, credit, real estate, and market solutions, and our unique strategy is driven by collaboration, innovation, and inclusion. Our teams combine deep product and sector experience with broad capabilities and expertise to develop differentiated insights and add value for our fund investors, portfolio companies, management teams, and communities.

TPG’s success depends on our people, and we build and sustain our world-class team by creating an inclusive, supportive culture within the firm that seeks excellence and encourages humility and transparency. The quality of our investments and our ability to build great companies depend on the originality of our insights. Reaching our firm’s full potential means supporting every team member to bring the fullness of their unique perspective to their work and to our community. We are committed to a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace to foster diversity of thought and reflect the breadth of our limited partners and portfolio companies.

Description of Position

The Project Coordinator is a high-visibility role supporting People Operations and the Office of the COO. This individual serves as an operational force multiplier, managing the workflow, data, and communications that drive leadership decision-making. The ideal candidate is a proactive problem-solver who can pivot between complex financial analysis and high-level executive storytelling.

Principal Responsibilities

• Draft sophisticated briefing notes, scripts, and presentations that accurately reflect the voice and priorities of the COO for leadership sessions, offsites, and external engagements.

• Transform scattered budget inputs and metrics into streamlined Excel models and dashboards that inform strategic shifts and provide decision-ready insights for leadership.

• Own the last mile of project execution by ensuring that decisions made in the boardroom are effectively communicated, tracked, and completed by functional owners.

• Direct the end-to-end logistics for leadership offsites and events, prioritizing a high-touch executive experience and seamless execution.

• Build and maintain comprehensive project plans and risk registers to proactively identify and mitigate potential slippage before it impacts the firm.

• Establish strategic agendas and facilitate working sessions, ensuring that concise recaps are circulated to drive accountability through clear ownership and due dates.

• Navigate a fast-paced environment with the ability to manage compressed deadlines and shifting priorities while focusing on outcome-ownership rather than task-completion.

• Utilize AI products and modern project management tools to optimize processes and increase the overall efficiency of the COO’s office.

• Execute special projects and administrative duties as assigned, including travel as required for leadership meetings and business priorities.

Requirements

• 2 – 4 years of experience in consulting, business operations, or a high-level executive support role.

• A bachelor’s degree is required, along with a strong interest in firm-wide operations and financial metrics.

• Expert-level proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel is necessary to produce client-ready work under tight deadlines.

• The role requires a high degree of discretion and professional judgment when handling confidential and sensitive information.

• A working knowledge of AI tools for research, drafting, and summarization is expected, along with the discernment to apply them effectively.

• Success in this role requires a candidate who thinks independently, resets quickly, and takes full ownership of outcomes.
